modules.purpose: Abstract base class every scanner extends; provides shared clean() and result assembly.
modules.behavior: Defines `abstract category: Category` and `abstract scan(options?)`. Shared `clean(items, dryRun=false)`: calls utils/fs `removeItems(items, dryRun)` which deletes items SEQUENTIALLY (one at a time, in given order). Aggregates failures by error code into ONE error string: `Failed to remove ${failed} items (${breakdown})` where breakdown is codes sorted by count descending, formatted like `32 EPERM, 3 EACCES` joined by ', '. Returns CleanResult {category, cleanedItems: successCount, freedSpace: sum of sizes of successfully-removed items, errors: []|[that one string]}. `createResult(items, error?)` returns ScanResult {category, items, totalSize: sum of item.size, error}. The underlying removeItemWithError (utils/fs.ts): on dryRun returns success immediately (so dryRun clean reports ALL items cleaned and FULL freedSpace); otherwise (1) validatePathSafety — refuses '/' ("Refusing to delete root directory"), refuses exact homedir, refuses protected paths, returning error code 'PROTECTED' and console.error-ing the message; (2) re-lstat immediately before delete (TOCTOU guard): if symlink → unlink() the link only (never follow); else `rm(path, {recursive:true, force:true})` (force = missing file is not an error... actually ENOENT still surfaces via lstat throwing first, returning code 'ENOENT'). On error returns errno code string ('EPERM','EACCES','ENOENT',...) or 'UNKNOWN'; only codes OTHER than ENOENT/EACCES/EPERM are console.error-logged. PROTECTED_PATHS (never delete, checked as exact match or prefix+'/'): /System, /usr, /bin, /sbin, /etc, /var/log, /var/db, /var/root, /private/var/db, /private/var/root, /private/var/log, /Library/Apple, /Applications/Utilities. ALLOWED_PATHS override (checked FIRST, always deletable): /tmp, /private/tmp, /var/tmp, /private/var/tmp, /var/folders, /private/var/folders. Paths are resolve()d (absolutized/normalized) before both checks.
modules.portingNotes: Go: os.RemoveAll for dirs, os.Remove for symlinks after os.Lstat type re-check. Map Go syscall errors to errno-code strings (EPERM/EACCES/ENOENT) to keep the failure-breakdown UX. Keep deletion sequential (or make progress-callback-safe). Note: because /var/log is in PROTECTED_PATHS, items scanned from /var/log by system-logs can never actually be deleted — every clean returns 'PROTECTED'. Preserve or consciously fix this quirk. dryRun must count all items as cleaned with full freedSpace.

modules.purpose: Lists per-app cache folders in the user cache directory.
modules.behavior: Scans exactly one path: ~/Library/Caches (PATHS.userCaches). If it exists, calls getDirectoryItems() which returns the IMMEDIATE children only (one CleanableItem per child: path, name = entry name, isDirectory, modifiedAt = lstat mtime, size = for dirs the FULL recursive logical size via getDirectorySize, for files/symlinks the lstat size — symlinks counted at link size, never followed). No age/size filters. clean() = base class rm -rf per selected child. Category: id 'system-cache', name 'User Cache Files', group 'System Junk', safetyLevel 'moderate', safetyNote 'Some apps may need to rebuild cache on next launch'. Note /Library/Caches (PATHS.systemCaches) is defined in paths.ts but NOT scanned.
modules.portingNotes: Directory sizing = recursive sum of lstat sizes (logical size, not disk blocks/du). Skip unreadable entries silently (return 0 / skip on error). Some ~/Library/Caches subdirs (e.g. CloudKit, com.apple.*) may be TCC-protected; deletion errors surface as EPERM counts — that's expected behavior.

modules.purpose: Lists user and system log files/folders.
modules.behavior: Scans two paths, immediate children each via getDirectoryItems: (1) ~/Library/Logs (PATHS.userLogs); (2) /var/log (PATHS.systemLogs) — wrapped in try/catch for permission failures (getDirectoryItems itself also swallows errors and returns []). No filters. clean() = base class. CRITICAL QUIRK: /var/log and /private/var/log are in PROTECTED_PATHS, so any item under /var/log fails deletion with 'PROTECTED' — scan shows them, clean refuses them. Category: 'System Log Files', group 'System Junk', safetyLevel 'moderate', safetyNote 'Logs may be useful for debugging issues'.
modules.portingNotes: Reading /var/log contents typically works without root on macOS but many files are root-owned; sizes of unreadable subtrees come back as 0. Decide in the Go port whether to keep listing /var/log items that can never be cleaned (TS behavior) or drop them — flag in UI at minimum.

modules.purpose: Lists temporary files in /tmp and the per-user /var/folders temp dirs.
modules.behavior: Scans: (1) /tmp (PATHS.tmp) — immediate children via getDirectoryItems. (2) /private/var/folders (PATHS.varFolders): iterates two directory levels — readdir(/private/var/folders) → for each dir1, readdir(/private/var/folders/<dir1>) → for each dir2, checks /private/var/folders/<dir1>/<dir2>/T; if that 'T' dir exists, lists ITS immediate children via getDirectoryItems. So items are children of .../T, e.g. /private/var/folders/ab/xyz123/T/com.apple.foo. Permission errors at any level are silently skipped. No filters. clean() = base class; both /tmp and /private/var/folders are in ALLOWED_PATHS so deletion is permitted by the safety check. Category: 'Temporary Files', group 'System Junk', safetyLevel 'safe'.
modules.portingNotes: On macOS /tmp is a symlink to /private/tmp — Node's readdir follows it transparently; in Go, os.ReadDir('/tmp') also works. Many items under /var/folders/.../T are owned by other users or in-use; expect lots of EPERM/EACCES — keep the silent-skip + error-count behavior. Some entries are sockets/pipes; getSize returns 0 for them (neither file, dir, nor symlink).

modules.purpose: Lists items in the user Trash.
modules.behavior: Scans exactly ~/.Trash (PATHS.trash), immediate children via getDirectoryItems (each item fully sized recursively). No filters. clean() = base class rm -rf per item (permanent delete, not 'empty trash' via Finder). Category: 'Trash', group 'Storage', safetyLevel 'safe'.
modules.portingNotes: Reading ~/.Trash requires Full Disk Access on modern macOS (TCC-protected); without FDA readdir fails and scanner silently returns 0 items. The Go/Wails app should detect this and prompt for FDA (the project has utils/fda.ts for this in the CLI).

modules.purpose: Lists old files in the Downloads folder.
modules.behavior: Scans ~/Downloads (PATHS.downloads) via getItems with {minAge: options.daysOld ?? 30, recursive: false}. Non-recursive: immediate children only, but child directories are sized recursively. Age filter: item included only if (now - lstat mtime) >= minAge days (computed as ms/(1000*60*60*24), fractional compare — `daysOld < minAge` skips). Uses lstat, so symlinks counted at link size. No dot-file exclusion here (getItems does not skip dotfiles). clean() = base class. Category: 'Old Downloads', group 'Storage', safetyLevel 'risky', safetyNote 'May contain important files you forgot about', supportsFileSelection: true (UI lets user pick individual files).
modules.portingNotes: options.daysOld is user-configurable; default 30. Age is based on mtime of the entry itself (for dirs, the dir's own mtime, not newest content). ~/Downloads read access may require TCC permission for a GUI app (Files and Folders prompt) — Wails will trigger the standard macOS consent dialog.

modules.purpose: Reports the whole cache directory of four known browsers as single items.
modules.behavior: Fixed list, each becomes ONE CleanableItem (isDirectory:true, size = full recursive size, modifiedAt = stat mtime of the dir) if the path exists: (1) 'Google Chrome' → ~/Library/Caches/Google/Chrome (the WHOLE Chrome caches tree, all profiles — note PATHS.chromeCacheDefault = ~/Library/Caches/Google/Chrome/Default/Cache exists in paths.ts but is UNUSED); (2) 'Safari' → ~/Library/Caches/com.apple.Safari; (3) 'Firefox' → ~/Library/Caches/Firefox/Profiles; (4) 'Arc' → ~/Library/Caches/company.thebrowser.Browser. Item name = `${browser.name} Cache` (e.g. 'Google Chrome Cache'). No size>0 filter — a 0-byte existing dir is still listed. Errors per browser are swallowed (continue). clean() = base class rm -rf of the whole cache dir. Category: 'Browser Cache', group 'Browsers', safetyLevel 'safe'.
modules.portingNotes: ~/Library/Caches/com.apple.Safari is TCC-protected — reading it requires Full Disk Access; without it the exists() check fails and Safari is silently omitted. Deleting Chrome cache while Chrome runs is allowed by the code (no running-process check) — consider warning in the GUI. Uses stat (follows symlink) for mtime but getSize uses lstat internally.

modules.purpose: Reports developer tool caches (package managers + Xcode).
modules.behavior: Part 1 — fixed single-item paths, included only if exists AND recursive size > 0: 'npm cache' → ~/.npm/_cacache; 'Yarn cache' → ~/Library/Caches/Yarn; 'pnpm store' → ~/Library/pnpm/store; 'pip cache' → ~/.cache/pip; 'CocoaPods cache' → ~/Library/Caches/CocoaPods; 'Gradle cache' → ~/.gradle/caches; 'Cargo cache' → ~/.cargo/registry. Each is one item (isDirectory:true, modifiedAt = stat mtime). Part 2 — ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData: getDirectoryItems → one item PER CHILD (per-project DerivedData folder), name rewritten to `Xcode: ${childName}`; NO size>0 filter here. Part 3 — ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/Archives as ONE item named 'Xcode Archives' if exists and size>0. PATHS.xcodeSimulators (~/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Devices) is defined but NOT scanned. clean() = base class rm -rf. Category: 'Development Cache', group 'Development', safetyLevel 'moderate', safetyNote 'Projects will need to rebuild/reinstall dependencies'.
modules.portingNotes: Straightforward filesystem work; sizes on ~/.gradle/caches and ~/.cargo/registry can be huge — do sizing concurrently in Go for speed. DerivedData child names look like 'MyApp-abcdefgh...' — keep the 'Xcode: ' prefix convention. Deleting ~/.npm/_cacache while npm runs is safe (content-addressed cache).

modules.purpose: Reports the Homebrew download cache and cleans via `brew cleanup`.
modules.behavior: Binary discovery (NEVER uses $PATH — anti-hijack): checks X_OK access in order on /opt/homebrew/bin/brew (Apple Silicon), /usr/local/bin/brew (Intel), /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew (Linux); first executable wins; none → empty result. Scan: runs `<brew> --cache` (spawn with args array, no shell, 30s timeout, stdio ignore/pipe/pipe; nonzero exit → reject with stderr). Trims stdout to get cache path, then SECURITY-VALIDATES it: path.resolve()d result must equal or be under (prefix+'/') one of: ~/Library/Caches/Homebrew, /opt/homebrew/Caches, /usr/local/Caches; otherwise console.warn(`Unexpected Homebrew cache location: ${path}`) and return empty. If valid, exists, and recursive size > 0: ONE item {path: cachePath, name: 'Homebrew Download Cache', isDirectory: true, modifiedAt: stat mtime}. clean(items, dryRun): dryRun → return {cleanedItems: items.length, freedSpace: sum sizes, errors: []} without doing anything. Else re-find brew if needed; if no brew → fall back to super.clean (direct rm -rf). Re-runs `brew --cache`; if the selected items include an item whose path EXACTLY equals the current brew cache root → runs `<brew> cleanup --prune=all`; freedSpace reported as the PRE-COMPUTED sum of item sizes (not measured after), cleanedItems = items.length on success, 0 on failure with error `Homebrew cleanup failed: <message>`. If cache root NOT among selected items → super.clean (direct deletion of whatever was selected).
modules.portingNotes: Go: exec.CommandContext with 30s timeout, absolute binary path, no shell. `brew cleanup --prune=all` also removes old versioned kegs/downloads — more thorough than rm of the cache dir; keep both paths (brew command when the cache-root item is selected, direct rm fallback otherwise). brew can be slow (>30s on big caches) — consider a longer timeout for cleanup than for --cache. Keep the cache-path allowlist validation verbatim.

modules.purpose: Reports Docker reclaimable space via `docker system df` and cleans via `docker system prune -af`.
modules.behavior: Binary discovery (allowlist, never $PATH): X_OK check in order on /usr/local/bin/docker, /opt/homebrew/bin/docker, /Applications/Docker.app/Contents/Resources/bin/docker; none → empty result. Scan: `<docker> system df --format '{{.Type}}\t{{.Size}}\t{{.Reclaimable}}'` (spawn, args array, 30s timeout). Parses each stdout line split on '\t' as [type, _, reclaimable]. Type is lowercased+trimmed and MUST be one of ['images','containers','local volumes','build cache'] (validation/injection guard) else line skipped. Reclaimable parsed with regex /([\d.]+)\s*(B|KB|MB|GB|TB|kB)/i and BINARY multipliers: B=1, KB=1024, MB=1024^2, GB=1024^3, TB=1024^4 (unknown unit → x1). Note: Docker actually prints SI/decimal units (kB/GB = 1000-based) but this code treats them as 1024-based — port as-is or consciously fix. Items only when reclaimable > 0: {path: `docker:${type with whitespace→'-'}` e.g. 'docker:images', 'docker:local-volumes', 'docker:build-cache'; size: reclaimableBytes; name: `Docker ${originalType}`; isDirectory: false; no modifiedAt}. Any error (docker not installed/daemon down) → silently empty result. clean(items, dryRun): dryRun → report all cleaned + full size sum, no action. Else find docker (error 'Docker binary not found in safe locations' if none), run `<docker> system prune -af` — INTENTIONALLY WITHOUT --volumes to prevent data loss (even though scan lists 'local volumes' reclaimable space; pruning will NOT actually free volume space). freedSpace = pre-computed sum of selected item sizes; cleanedItems = items.length if no error else 0; failure → error `Docker cleanup failed: <message>`.
modules.portingNotes: Items have virtual 'docker:*' paths — the generic filesystem clean must never receive them; Docker overrides clean() entirely. Note prune -af runs regardless of WHICH docker items the user selected (all-or-nothing; it can't prune only build cache). 30s timeout may be too short for a big prune — consider raising for clean in Go. Docker Desktop must be running; handle 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon' stderr as the silent-empty case on scan but a reported error on clean.

modules.purpose: Lists iOS/iPadOS device backups.
modules.behavior: Scans ~/Library/Application Support/MobileSync/Backup (PATHS.iosBackups). Immediate children via getDirectoryItems — each child is a device backup dir (40-hex-char UDID name), fully sized recursively. Name rewritten to `iOS Backup: ${first 8 chars of dir name}...` (substring(0,8) + literal '...'). clean() = base class rm -rf of the backup dir. Category: 'iOS Backups', group 'Storage', safetyLevel 'risky', safetyNote 'DANGER: You may lose important device backups permanently!'.
modules.portingNotes: ~/Library/Application Support/MobileSync is TCC-protected: requires Full Disk Access to even list; without FDA the scanner silently returns 0 items. Backup dirs contain tens of thousands of small files — recursive sizing is the slowest part; parallelize in Go.

modules.purpose: Lists Mail.app downloaded attachments.
modules.behavior: Scans ~/Library/Containers/com.apple.mail/Data/Library/Mail Downloads (PATHS.mailDownloads). Immediate children via getDirectoryItems (typically UUID-named folders each containing one attachment), fully sized. No filters, names kept as-is. clean() = base class. Category: 'Mail Attachments', group 'Storage', safetyLevel 'risky', safetyNote 'May contain important documents and files'.
modules.portingNotes: The com.apple.mail container is TCC-protected — Full Disk Access required or the exists() check fails silently. Path contains a space ('Mail Downloads') — no quoting issues in Go since no shell is involved.

modules.purpose: Finds unused .lproj localization folders inside /Applications app bundles.
modules.behavior: readdir('/Applications'); for each entry whose name ends with '.app' (top level only — no subfolder recursion, no ~/Applications): check <app>/Contents/Resources exists; readdir it; select entries ending '.lproj' whose base name (with '.lproj' stripped) is NOT in KEEP_LANGUAGES = ['en','en_US','en_GB','pt','pt_BR','pt_PT','Base'] (note: pt variants kept because the author is Portuguese-speaking — make this configurable in the port). Each match becomes an item: path = /Applications/<app>.app/Contents/Resources/<lang>.lproj, size = recursive size, name = `${app}: ${lproj}` (app includes the '.app' suffix, e.g. 'Slack.app: fr.lproj'), isDirectory: true, modifiedAt = stat mtime. Per-app and per-lproj errors silently skipped. clean() = base class rm -rf of each .lproj dir. Category: 'Language Files', group 'System Junk', safetyLevel 'risky', safetyNote 'May break apps if you switch system language'.
modules.portingNotes: Deleting inside /Applications bundles: (1) often requires admin rights for apps installed by installers (root-owned) — expect EPERM/EACCES failures reported via the error breakdown, TS does NOT use sudo; (2) BREAKS code signatures — signed/notarized apps may fail to launch or trigger Gatekeeper re-verification after modification; some apps (App Store, SIP-adjacent) are unmodifiable. The Go port should surface these caveats. Matching is case-sensitive ('EN.lproj' would not be kept).

modules.purpose: Finds individual files >= 500MB in Downloads and Documents for manual review.
modules.behavior: minSize = options.minSize ?? SIZE_THRESHOLDS.LARGE_FILE = 500 * 1024 * 1024 (524,288,000 bytes). Search roots: ~/Downloads and ~/Documents. Recursive walk with maxDepth = 3, semantics: root call has currentDepth 0, recursion increments, and `if (currentDepth > maxDepth) return` — so directories at depth 0..3 (relative to each root) are read; files up to 4 path components below the root are found. Skips any entry whose name starts with '.' (files and dirs). Only regular files (readdir withFileTypes: symlinks are neither isFile nor isDirectory → skipped entirely). For each file, stat() (follows symlinks, but symlinks never reach here); include if stats.size >= minSize; item {path, size, name: filename only, isDirectory: false, modifiedAt}. Per-entry and per-dir errors silently skipped. Final list sorted by size DESCENDING. clean() = base class. Category: 'Large Files', group 'Large Files', safetyLevel 'risky', safetyNote 'Review each file carefully before deleting', supportsFileSelection: true.
modules.portingNotes: In Go use os.ReadDir (DirEntry.Type() is Lstat-based, matching Node dirent semantics — symlinks excluded). Keep exact depth semantics (off-by-one matters: maxDepth 3 means 4 levels of files). Dot-dir skip means ~/Documents/.hidden trees are never scanned.

modules.purpose: Finds node_modules folders in stale or orphaned projects under common dev directories.
modules.behavior: Search roots (only those that exist): ~/Projects, ~/Developer, ~/Code, ~/dev, ~/workspace, ~/repos. daysOld = options.daysOld ?? 30. Recursive walk, maxDepth = 4 (same depth semantics as large-files: dirs at depth 0..4 read). Skips non-directories and names starting with '.'. When a directory named exactly 'node_modules' is found: (A) check `access(parentDir/package.json)`. If package.json EXISTS: compute daysSinceModified = (now - parentDir lstat... actually stat mtime)/86400000 (fractional); include the node_modules dir ONLY if daysSinceModified >= daysOld, with size = full recursive size (even if 0), name = `${lastPathComponentOfParentDir} (${Math.floor(days)}d old)`. (B) If package.json MISSING (access throws) → 'orphaned': include regardless of age but only if recursive size > 0, name = `${parentDirName} (orphaned)`. In both cases isDirectory: true, modifiedAt = node_modules stat mtime. Never recurses INTO a node_modules dir. Sibling dirs keep being walked. Per-dir errors silently ignored. Final sort by size DESCENDING. clean() = base class rm -rf of the node_modules dir only (project sources untouched). Category: 'Node Modules', group 'Development', safetyLevel 'moderate', safetyNote 'Projects will need npm install to restore'.
modules.portingNotes: Staleness is judged by the PROJECT dir's mtime, not node_modules' — note a project dir's mtime only changes when direct children are added/removed, so 'age' is a rough heuristic; port verbatim. The catch block treats ANY error (not just missing package.json) as 'orphaned' — e.g. permission error on access() → labeled orphaned; replicate or improve deliberately. Recursive sizing of many node_modules is the hot path — parallelize with a worker pool in Go.

modules.purpose: Finds byte-identical duplicate files in Downloads, Documents, Desktop; keeps the newest copy.
modules.behavior: Search roots: ~/Downloads, ~/Documents, ~/Desktop. minSize = options.minSize ?? MIN_FILE_SIZE = 1024*1024 (1 MiB). Walk: recursive, MAX_DEPTH = 5 (`currentDepth > maxDepth` → return; root call depth 0). Skips entries starting with '.'. Only regular files (dirent.isFile(); symlinks skipped). Phase 1 — group by exact byte size: Map<size, FileInfo[]> where FileInfo = {path, size, modifiedAt} from stat. Phase 2 — for every size group with >= 2 files: compute FULL-FILE MD5 hex hash of each (utils/hash.ts getFileHash, streaming createReadStream + crypto md5; per-file hash errors → file skipped). Regroup by hash; any hash group with >= 2 files is a duplicate set. (Note: getFileHashPartial(first 1MB) exists in utils/hash.ts but is UNUSED — an intended optimization never wired up.) Phase 3 — per duplicate set: sort files by modifiedAt DESCENDING; the newest is KEPT (never listed); every older file becomes a CleanableItem {path, size, name: `${basename} (dup of ${basenameOfNewest})`, isDirectory: false, modifiedAt}. Final items sorted by size DESCENDING. clean() = base class (deletes only the older copies the user confirms). Category: 'Duplicate Files', group 'Storage', safetyLevel 'risky', safetyNote 'Review carefully - keeps newest copy by default'.
modules.portingNotes: Go: crypto/md5 + io.Copy; hashing is sequential in TS — parallelize with a bounded worker pool but keep deterministic 'newest kept' selection (tie-break: TS sort is stable, first-encountered order wins on equal mtimes). Consider adding the partial-hash pre-filter (hash first 1 MiB, only full-hash on partial match) as the TS code clearly intended. basename extraction is split('/') last segment.

modules.purpose: Finds user LaunchAgent plists whose target program no longer exists (orphaned).
modules.behavior: Scans ~/Library/LaunchAgents only (not /Library/LaunchAgents or LaunchDaemons). Missing dir → empty result. readdir failure → ScanResult with error `Failed to read LaunchAgents directory: <message>`. Filters files ending '.plist'. For each plist: reads it as UTF-8 TEXT and extracts the program path via regex (NOT a real plist parser): first tries /<key>Program<\/key>\s*<string>([^<]+)<\/string>/, else /<key>ProgramArguments<\/key>\s*<array>\s*<string>([^<]+)<\/string>/ (first array element); result trimmed. Skip if: no program found (or binary plist — regex won't match, silently skipped); path is not absolute; path starts with a SYSTEM_BINARY_PREFIXES entry: /usr/bin/, /bin/, /sbin/, /usr/sbin/, /usr/local/bin/, /opt/homebrew/bin/ (these are assumed managed/valid, never 'orphaned'). Orphaned test: `exists(programPath)` fails (fs access). Orphaned items: {path: the plist file, size: plist file size (bytes, tiny), name: `${plistFile} → ${programPath} (missing)` (uses Unicode arrow ' → '), isDirectory: false, modifiedAt: plist mtime}. Per-plist errors → skip. clean() = base class: deletes the .plist file only — does NOT run `launchctl unload/bootout`, so the agent stays loaded until logout/reboot. Category: 'Orphaned Launch Agents', group 'System Junk', safetyLevel 'moderate', safetyNote 'Removing launch agents will prevent applications from auto-starting. Only orphaned items (pointing to non-existent apps) are detected.'.
modules.portingNotes: The regex approach misses binary plists (bplist00) — Go should use howett.net/plist which parses both XML and binary, improving coverage; but preserve the same skip rules (no program key, relative path, system-binary prefix). The regex also requires exact whitespace order <key>…</key> then <string> — real-world XML plists match, but comments between tags would break TS parsing; a real parser in Go is strictly better. Consider optionally running `launchctl bootout gui/$UID <plist>` before deletion in the port (TS does not).

modules.purpose: Scanner registry and parallel scan orchestrator.
modules.behavior: ALL_SCANNERS: Record<CategoryId, Scanner> with 16 singleton instances in this order: system-cache, system-logs, temp-files, trash, downloads, browser-cache, dev-cache, homebrew, docker, ios-backups, mail-attachments, language-files, large-files, node-modules, duplicates, launch-agents. getScanner(id) throws `Unknown scanner category: ${id}` if missing. runAllScans(options, onProgress) = runScans(all ids, ...). runScans(categoryIds, options, onProgress): parallel = options.parallel ?? true; concurrency = options.concurrency ?? 4, clamped to max(1, min(concurrency, taskCount)). Custom concurrency pool (runWithConcurrency): starts tasks up to the limit, `await Promise.race(executing)` when full; a FAILED scanner task is console.error-logged (`Scanner task (<categoryId>) failed:`) and its result is FILTERED OUT of the summary (not an error entry — silently dropped). Progress: after each scan completes, increments `completed` and calls BOTH options.onProgress(completed, total, scanner, result) and the second-arg onProgress(scanner, result). Sequential mode (parallel=false): simple for-loop, same callbacks. Returns ScanSummary {results, totalSize: sum of result.totalSize, totalItems: sum of result.items.length}. Also re-exports every scanner class.
modules.portingNotes: Go: errgroup + semaphore (weight 4) or buffered-channel worker pool; deliver progress to the Wails frontend via runtime.EventsEmit since the completed counter is shared — guard with atomic/mutex. Preserve 'failed scanner is dropped, not fatal' semantics. Scanner instances are stateful for docker/homebrew (they cache the discovered binary path between scan and clean) — keep one long-lived instance per category in the Go app struct.

scanners.crossCutting: CONTRACTS (types.ts): CleanableItem {path string; size int64 bytes; name string (display); isDirectory bool; modifiedAt time optional}. ScanResult {category, items, totalSize = sum(items.size), error? string}. CleanResult {category, cleanedItems int, freedSpace int64, errors []string}. ScannerOptions {verbose?, daysOld?, minSize?} — the SAME options object is passed to every scanner in a batch run (daysOld feeds downloads + node-modules; minSize feeds large-files + duplicates). Scanner interface: category + scan(options) + clean(items, dryRun). CATEGORIES metadata drives the UI: safetyLevel ('safe'|'moderate'|'risky'), safetyNote, group ('System Junk'|'Development'|'Storage'|'Browsers'|'Large Files'), supportsFileSelection (true only for downloads and large-files). DELETION PIPELINE (utils/fs.ts — shared by all except docker/homebrew overrides): sequential removeItems; per item: (1) dryRun → instant success, full freedSpace credited; (2) validatePathSafety: resolve() path, refuse '/', refuse homedir exactly, refuse PROTECTED_PATHS [/System, /usr, /bin, /sbin, /etc, /var/log, /var/db, /var/root, /private/var/db, /private/var/root, /private/var/log, /Library/Apple, /Applications/Utilities] (exact or prefix+'/') UNLESS under ALLOWED_PATHS [/tmp, /private/tmp, /var/tmp, /private/var/tmp, /var/folders, /private/var/folders] which are checked first and always win → refusals return code 'PROTECTED'; (3) TOCTOU guard: re-lstat right before delete; symlink → unlink link only (never follow); else rm recursive+force. Failures collected as errno-code strings and summarized by BaseScanner as one message: 'Failed to remove N items (32 EPERM, 3 EACCES)' sorted by count desc. SIZING (utils/fs.ts): all sizes are LOGICAL lstat sizes (not disk usage/blocks); symlinks counted at the link's own size, never followed; directory size = recursive sum, unreadable subtrees contribute 0; sockets/pipes/devices contribute 0. getDirectoryItems(dir) = immediate children each fully sized — the workhorse for system-cache/system-logs/temp-files/trash/ios-backups/mail-attachments. getItems(dir, {recursive=false, minAge days via mtime, minSize, maxDepth=10}) — used only by downloads. EXTERNAL COMMANDS (docker.ts/homebrew.ts pattern): binaries located ONLY via hardcoded absolute-path allowlists with X_OK checks (never $PATH — hijack prevention); executed via spawn with argv arrays (no shell, no injection), 30,000 ms timeout, stdio ['ignore','pipe','pipe']; nonzero exit rejects with stderr text; command outputs are validated against allowlists before trust (docker df types, brew cache path prefixes). Both override clean() and report freedSpace as the pre-scan size sum, not a measured delta, and both short-circuit dryRun to full success. DEPTH SEMANTICS (recursive scanners): root call depth 0, guard is `currentDepth > maxDepth`, so dirs at depth 0..maxDepth are read (large-files maxDepth 3, node-modules 4, duplicates 5); all three skip dot-entries and skip symlinks (dirent type checks are lstat-based — mirror with Go os.ReadDir DirEntry.Type()). ERROR PHILOSOPHY: scan errors are swallowed per-entry/per-path (silent skip, empty result); a scanner never throws out of scan() except via ScanResult.error; the orchestrator drops (does not fail on) a rejected scanner. FORMAT: sizes formatted base-1024 with units B/KB/MB/GB/TB, one decimal above bytes (utils/size.ts); SIZE_THRESHOLDS: LARGE_FILE 500 MiB, MEDIUM_FILE 100 MiB, SMALL_FILE 10 MiB. macOS PERMISSIONS FOR THE WAILS PORT: Full Disk Access needed to see ~/.Trash, Safari caches (com.apple.Safari), MobileSync iOS backups, and the com.apple.mail container — without FDA these scanners silently return empty; the CLI has a utils/fda.ts helper that the GUI should replace with an FDA-detection + System Settings deep-link flow. No sudo is ever used; root-owned files simply fail with EPERM and are counted in the error breakdown.

modules.purpose: Default guided flow: scan all categories, drill-down file-picker selection, confirm, clean, print results.
modules.behavior: Options: {includeRisky?, noProgress?, absolutePaths?, filePicker?}. Step-by-step: (0) Prints header '🧹 Mac Cleaner CLI' + dim 50-char '─' rule. Then calls hasFullDiskAccess() (from utils); if it returns exactly false, prints yellow FULL_DISK_ACCESS_HINT once (one-time hint instead of dozens of EPERM errors later, referencing issue #61). (1) SCAN: showProgress = !noProgress && process.stdout.isTTY; progress bar via createScanProgress(scannerCount). Prints cyan 'Scanning your Mac for cleanable files...'. Runs runAllScans({parallel: true, concurrency: 4, onProgress}) where onProgress updates bar with 'Scanning {category.name}...'. If summary.totalSize === 0 → green '✓ Your Mac is already clean! Nothing to remove.' and return null. (2) FILTER: keep results with items.length > 0; split into risky (category.safetyLevel === 'risky') vs safe. If !includeRisky and risky exist: print yellow '⚠ Hiding risky categories:' then per risky category dim '  {redDot} {name}: {formatSize(totalSize)}', then dim '  Total hidden: {size}' and dim '  Run with --risky to include these categories'; drop risky results. If nothing left → green '✓ Nothing safe to clean!' return null. (3) Print bold 'Found {green formatSize(summary.totalSize)} that can be cleaned:'. (4) SELECT via filePickerPrompt with message 'Select categories to clean (space to toggle, enter to confirm):'. categoriesWithFileSelection = ALL category ids when options.filePicker (-f flag) is true, otherwise only categories where category.supportsFileSelection is true. After the prompt returns {selectedCategories: Set, selectedFilesByCategory: Map<CategoryId, Set<path>>}: for each selected category — if it is in categoriesWithFileSelection, include only result.items whose item.path is in the selected file set (skip category entirely if set is empty/missing); otherwise include ALL of the category's items. If final selection empty → yellow 'No items selected. Nothing to clean.' return null. (5) CONFIRM: prints bold 'Summary:' with '  Items to delete: {yellow N}' and '  Space to free: {green size}', then @inquirer/confirm 'Proceed with cleaning?' with DEFAULT TRUE (note: clean command defaults false). Declined → yellow 'Cleaning cancelled.' return null. (6) CLEAN: createCleanProgress(selectedCategoryCount); sequential loop over selected {categoryId, items}: progress 'Cleaning {name}...', await scanner.clean(items) (no dryRun arg here), accumulate freedSpace/cleanedItems/errors.length into CleanSummary {results, totalFreedSpace, totalCleanedItems, totalErrors}. (7) RESULTS: bold green '✓ Cleaning Complete!' + dim rule; per result with cleanedItems>0: '  {name.padEnd(30)} ✓ {formatSize(freedSpace)} freed'; each error as '  {name.padEnd(30)} ✗ {error}'; footer bold '🎉 Freed {green size} of disk space!' + dim '   Cleaned {N} items' + red '   Errors: {N}' if any. NO donation prompt in interactive (only clean command has it). Returns CleanSummary. SAFETY_ICONS: safe=green '●', moderate=yellow '●', risky=red '●'.
modules.portingNotes: hasFullDiskAccess()/FULL_DISK_ACCESS_HINT live in src/utils (not read here) — in Wails, surface Full Disk Access status in the UI; the Go binary needs FDA granted in System Settings > Privacy & Security to read ~/Library/Mail, Safari data, etc., otherwise expect EPERM on many scanner paths. TTY/noProgress logic becomes irrelevant in Wails (replace with event-based progress: emit completed/total/currentCategoryName). Confirm default=true here vs default=false in clean.ts — preserve the asymmetry deliberately or unify. Cleaning is strictly sequential per category (one scanner.clean at a time) even though scanning is concurrency-4; keep that ordering so progress and error attribution stay per-category.

modules.purpose: Scriptable clean command with --all/--yes/--dry-run/--categories/--unsafe semantics plus a simpler two-level checkbox fallback UI and a donation prompt.
modules.behavior: Options: {all?, yes?, dryRun?, categories?: CategoryId[], unsafe?, noProgress?}. Flow: categoryIds = options.categories if non-empty else all scanner ids. Scan with {parallel: true, concurrency: 4, onProgress→'Scanning {name}...'}; uses runScans(categoryIds) when --categories given, else runAllScans. totalSize===0 → green '✓ Your Mac is already clean!' return null. Risky gating: unless --unsafe, prints yellow '⚠ Skipping risky categories (use --unsafe to include):', per category dim '  {redDot} {name}: {size}' plus dim-italic safetyNote line '     {note}' if present, then dim '  Total skipped: {size}'; risky results removed. Empty after filter → green '✓ Nothing safe to clean!'. SELECTION: if options.all OR options.categories?.length → take ALL items of every remaining category non-interactively (explicit --categories deliberately behaves like --all scoped to those categories, so it works in scripts/cron); else selectItemsInteractively: first @inquirer/checkbox over categories (pageSize 15, all unchecked, choice name '{safetyIcon} {name.padEnd(28)} {yellow size.padStart(10)} ({n} items)', value=category.id); then, for each chosen category, IF category is risky OR category.supportsFileSelection: (if risky with safetyNote, print red '⚠ WARNING: {safetyNote}') then a second checkbox per item (pageSize 10, unchecked, name '{item.name.substring(0,40).padEnd(40)} {yellow size.padStart(10)}', value=item.path); category included only if ≥1 item picked. Non-risky non-file-selection categories include all items automatically. Empty selection → yellow 'No items selected for cleaning.' CONFIRM: only when !yes && !dryRun: confirm 'Delete {totalItems} items ({formatSize(totalToClean)})?' DEFAULT FALSE; declined → 'Cleaning cancelled.' DRY RUN: prints cyan '[DRY RUN] Would clean the following:' then per category '  {name}: {n} items ({size})' then cyan '[DRY RUN] Would free {size}'; returns null WITHOUT deleting anything (returns before the clean loop, so the dryRun flag passed to scanner.clean(items, options.dryRun) is effectively never true in practice). CLEAN: sequential loop; scanner.clean(items, options.dryRun); accumulate into CleanSummary. RESULTS: bold green '✓ Cleaning Complete' + dim 50-char rule; per-category '✓ {size} freed' / '✗ {error}' lines; 'Freed: {green size}', dim 'Cleaned {N} items', red 'Errors: {N}' if any. DONATION: if totalCleanedItems>0 && totalFreedSpace>0: prints '💚 Enjoying Mac Cleaner CLI?' with cyan underlined https://ko-fi.com/guhcostan; confirm 'Open donation page in browser?' default false; if yes → openUrl(): skipped when NODE_ENV==='test' || CI==='true' || !stdout.isTTY; validates URL parses and protocol is https: or http: (else console.error 'Invalid URL protocol'/'Invalid URL format'); then spawn('/usr/bin/open', [url], {detached: true, stdio: 'ignore'}).unref() — args passed separately to prevent command injection; prints green '✓ Opened in your browser. Thank you for your support!' or dim 'Thank you for using Mac Cleaner CLI!'.
modules.portingNotes: In Go use exec.Command("/usr/bin/open", url) (never a shell string) or Wails runtime BrowserOpenURL. Preserve the exact non-interactive contract for CLI parity: --categories implies select-everything-in-those-categories with no prompts, and dry-run never prompts nor deletes. Confirmation ordering matters: dryRun bypasses the confirm entirely. The dead dryRun parameter to scanner.clean can be dropped in the port. The donation gate (cleanedItems>0 AND freedSpace>0) and env-based suppression need Go equivalents (os.Getenv("CI"), test detection).

modules.purpose: Read-only scan with grouped terminal report, --json machine output, and the `list categories` helper.
modules.behavior: Options: {category?: CategoryId (single), verbose?, noProgress?, json?}. showProgress = !noProgress && !json && stdout.isTTY. Scans via runScans([category]) or runAllScans with {verbose, parallel: true, concurrency: 4, onProgress→'Scanning {name}...'}. JSON mode: JSON.stringify(obj, null, 2) of {totalSize, totalItems, categories: [only results with items.length>0] each {id, name, group, safetyLevel, totalSize, itemCount, items?: [{path, size}]}} where items array is included ONLY with --verbose (kept small by default; documented for `scan --json | jq` scripting). Text mode printScanResults: bold 'Scan Results' + dim 60-char '─' rule; results grouped by category.group into a FIXED ordered record: 'System Junk', 'Development', 'Storage', 'Browsers', 'Large Files'; groups with groupTotal===0 skipped; within a group, categories with totalSize===0 skipped; line format '  {safetyIcon} {name.padEnd(28)} {yellow formatSize.padStart(10)} ({itemCount} items)'. With --verbose: top 5 items sorted size-desc printed as dim '      └─ {name.padEnd(24)} {size.padStart(10)}' plus dim '      └─ ... and {n-5} more' if more. Footer: dim 60-char rule, bold 'Total: {green size} can be cleaned ({N} items)', legend 'Safety: ● safe  ● moderate  ● risky (use --unsafe)'. listCategories(): bold 'Available Categories' + dim 70-char rule; iterates the CATEGORIES constant (from src/types.ts) grouped into the same 5 fixed groups; per category '  {icon} {yellow id.padEnd(18)} {dim description}' plus optional '       ⚠ {safetyNote}' dim-italic; legend says 'risky (requires --unsafe)'. Returns ScanSummary.
modules.portingNotes: The --json schema is a public scripting contract — replicate field names and the verbose-gated items array byte-compatibly (encoding/json with struct tags; note TS omits the items key entirely when not verbose, so use omitempty/pointer). The 5-group ordering is hardcoded and must be preserved (Go maps are unordered — use an ordered slice of group names). CATEGORIES metadata lives in src/types.ts and must be analyzed/ported separately.

modules.purpose: App uninstaller: enumerates .app bundles, discovers associated Library files via bundle-ID/app-name templates, and deletes app + leftovers.
modules.behavior: Options: {yes?, dryRun?, noProgress?}. APP DISCOVERY (getInstalledApps): scans exactly two dirs — '/Applications' and join(homedir(), 'Applications') — skipping any that don't exist. For each readdir entry ending '.app': appPath = dir/entry; appName = basename(entry, '.app'); stat must be a directory (else skip); appSize = getSize(appPath); relatedPaths = findRelatedPaths(appName, appPath); totalSize = appSize + sum(getSize(each related).catch(→0)). Per-entry and per-dir errors swallowed (continue). Result sorted by totalSize DESC. Not recursive — only top-level .app bundles. BUNDLE ID (getBundleId): reads {appPath}/Contents/Info.plist as UTF-8 TEXT and regex-matches /<key>CFBundleIdentifier<\/key>\s*<string>([^<]+)<\/string>/; trimmed value must match /^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9.-]*$/ else null; any error → null. Fallback when null: bundleId = appName.toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, '.'). RELATED PATH TEMPLATES (11, all under $HOME): ~/Library/Application Support/{APP_NAME}; ~/Library/Preferences/{BUNDLE_ID}.plist; ~/Library/Preferences/{APP_NAME}.plist; ~/Library/Caches/{APP_NAME}; ~/Library/Caches/{BUNDLE_ID}; ~/Library/Logs/{APP_NAME}; ~/Library/Saved Application State/{BUNDLE_ID}.savedState; ~/Library/WebKit/{APP_NAME}; ~/Library/HTTPStorages/{BUNDLE_ID}; ~/Library/Containers/{BUNDLE_ID}; ~/Library/Group Containers/*.{APP_NAME}. For EACH template, THREE variations tried: {APP_NAME} → (1) appName verbatim, (2) appName.toLowerCase(), (3) appName with all whitespace stripped (replace(/\s+/g,'')); {BUNDLE_ID} always the resolved bundleId. Safety per candidate: resolve() must startWith(home + '/') else skip; isProtectedPath(resolved) → skip. If path contains '*': dir = substring before last '/', pattern = after; if dir exists, readdir and matchPattern(entry, pattern) where matchPattern escapes ALL regex metachars via /[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g → '\\$&' then converts escaped \* to '.*' and tests case-insensitive anchored ^pattern$ (regex construction failure → false); matched fullPath added if !isProtectedPath and not already in list. Non-glob paths added if exists() and not duplicate. UI FLOW: cyan 'Scanning installed applications...'; if 0 apps → yellow 'No applications found.'. @inquirer/checkbox (pageSize 15, unchecked, value=app.name, choice name '{name.padEnd(35)} {yellow totalSize.padStart(10)} (+{relatedPaths.length} related)'). Zero picked → 'No applications selected.'. Preview: bold 'Applications to uninstall:'; per app '  ✗ {name} ({totalSize})' with each related path dim '      └─ {path with homedir→~}'; bold 'Total: {size} will be freed ({totalPaths} items)' where totalPaths = Σ(1 + relatedPaths.length). DRY RUN: cyan '[DRY RUN] Would uninstall the above applications.' and return — dry-run happens BEFORE the confirm, so it never prompts. CONFIRM (if !yes): 'Proceed with uninstallation?' default FALSE. DELETE LOOP (sequential, createCleanProgress(appCount), '(Uninstalling {name}...')): safeRemove(app.path) → validatePathSafety(path) first (non-null error string → console.error + return false); then lstat: symlink → unlink (do NOT follow); else rm(path, {recursive: true, force: true}). If the main .app removal fails → push error '{name}: Failed to remove (security check failed or permission denied)' and CONTINUE to next app (related paths NOT touched). On success: freedSpace += app.size; then each relatedPath safeRemove'd; if removed, size = await getSize(relatedPath).catch(→0) — NOTE this measures AFTER deletion so related-path freed space is systematically under-counted (existing bug; fix in port by summing before delete). uninstalledCount++ per successful app. Thrown errors get homedir replaced with '~' in the message. SUMMARY: bold green '✓ Uninstallation Complete' + dim 50-char rule; '  Apps uninstalled: {N}'; '  Space freed: {green size}'; red 'Errors:' list of '  ✗ {msg}'. IMPORTANT: there is NO running-application check anywhere — an open app is deleted without warning, and no `osascript quit`/pkill is attempted. No sudo/privilege escalation: /Applications deletions rely on the user owning the bundle; failures surface as the generic error string.
modules.portingNotes: Biggest gap for Go: Info.plist regex parsing only works for XML plists — most modern apps ship BINARY plists, so the TS version silently falls back to the name-guess bundle ID for them. In Go use howett.net/plist (handles both formats) or shell out to `plutil -convert xml1 -o -` / `defaults read <path> CFBundleIdentifier`; keep the /^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9.-]*$/ validation and the lowercase-dotted fallback for parity. isProtectedPath/validatePathSafety live in src/utils (not read here) and must be ported with this module — they are the only guardrails before recursive rm. Related-path search is home-only by design (resolve must start with home+'/'), so system-level leftovers (/Library/..., LaunchAgents/Daemons) are intentionally NOT touched — decide whether the Wails app extends this. Fix the size-after-delete bug. Consider adding the missing running-app check (NSRunningApplication via cgo/objc, or `pgrep -f {bundleId}` / `osascript -e 'quit app "X"'`). Deleting from /Applications may need admin rights or produce EPERM for system-installed apps; Wails should surface per-app errors, and TCC Full Disk Access is needed to enumerate/delete some ~/Library subpaths (Containers especially). lstat-symlink handling matters: use os.Lstat and os.Remove for symlinks, os.RemoveAll otherwise, to avoid following links out of the sandboxed target.

modules.purpose: Thin orchestrator running opt-in maintenance tasks (DNS flush, purgeable space, Time Machine snapshots) with spinner feedback.
modules.behavior: Options: {dns?, purgeable?, timemachine?} — each boolean maps to a task tuple: --dns → 'Flush DNS Cache' → flushDnsCache(); --purgeable → 'Free Purgeable Space' → freePurgeableSpace(); --timemachine → 'Clear Time Machine Snapshots' → clearTimeMachineSnapshots(). All three functions are imported from ../maintenance/index.js — their shell commands are NOT in this file and need separate analysis of src/maintenance/. If no flags given: yellow 'No maintenance tasks specified.' + dim 'Use --dns, --purgeable, or --timemachine for maintenance tasks.' and return. Otherwise prints bold 'Running Maintenance Tasks' + dim 50-char '─' rule, then runs tasks SEQUENTIALLY, each wrapped in an ora spinner started with the task name. Each task returns MaintenanceResult {success: boolean, message: string, error?: string}: success → spinner.succeed(green message); failure → spinner.fail(red '{message}: {error}') or spinner.fail(red message) when error absent. No confirmation prompts, no dry-run support here.
modules.portingNotes: The actual system commands live in src/maintenance/index.ts (unread) — expect typically `dscacheutil -flushcache` + `killall -HUP mDNSResponder` (needs sudo), `tmutil listlocalsnapshots /` + `tmutil deletelocalsnapshots <date>` for Time Machine, and some purge strategy; verify against the real source before porting, and note these likely require sudo/admin — a Wails GUI cannot inherit a terminal sudo prompt, so plan for osascript 'do shell script ... with administrator privileges' or an SMJobBless-style helper. ora spinner semantics map to per-task status events in Wails (running/success/fail with message+error).

modules.purpose: Custom @inquirer/core prompt: two-pane (categories + inline per-directory file drill-down) selector returning selected categories and per-category file path sets.
modules.behavior: Config {message, results: ScanResult[], absolutePaths?: boolean, categoriesWithFileSelection?: Set<CategoryId>} → Result {selectedCategories: Set<CategoryId>, selectedFilesByCategory: Map<CategoryId, Set<string(path)>>}. CONSTANTS: FILES_PAGE_SIZE=6 (centered pagination window), FILE_NAME_WIDTH=35 (truncation), INDENT='    ' (4 spaces), DIR_VIS_CHILD_LIMIT=5 (default files shown per directory), EXPAND_INCREMENT=10, GRAPH_MIN_WIDTH=0.2, GRAPH_MAX_WIDTH=20, GRAPH_FRACTIONS=['▏','▎','▍','▌','█']. Size bar renderSizeGraph(size, largestSize): ratio=size/largest (0 if largest 0); scaled=max(ratio*20, 0.2); fullBlocks=floor(scaled); fractionIndex=min(floor((scaled-fullBlocks)*5), 4); bar='█'.repeat(fullBlocks) + (fullBlocks<20 ? GRAPH_FRACTIONS[fractionIndex] : ''). STATE: activePane ∈ {'categories','files'}; categoryCaret; selectedCategories: Set; selectedFilesByCategory: Map; copyStatus: string|null; per-category FilePickerState {visible: bool (files shown inline), active: bool (keyboard focus inside this picker; only ONE may be active), fileCaret: number, dirExpandLimits: Record<directoryKey, number>} stored in a Record keyed by String(categoryId), defaulting to {visible:false, active:false, fileCaret:0, dirExpandLimits:{}}. Grouped display lists computed per file-selection category via groupFilesByDirectory(result.items, absolutePaths, limitsMap) from src/utils/grouping.ts (pipeline per README: groupByDirectory sorts dirs by size desc → applyExpandLimits → formatAsDisplayItems), producing GroupedFileDisplay rows of type 'directory-header' (non-selectable, has displayName + totalFilesInDir), 'file' (selectable, has item {path,...}, displayName, size, directoryKey), 'expand-hint' (non-selectable '+N more files' row with hiddenCount + directoryKey). KEYMAP — Enter (both panes): write '\x1B[?25h' (re-show cursor) then done(selections). Categories pane: up/down move caret clamped [0, results.length-1]; SPACE toggles category — deselect: remove id, and for file-selection categories set its file set to EMPTY set and pickerState.visible=false; select: add id, and for file-selection categories AUTO-SELECT ALL item paths and visible=true. 'a': if every category selected → clear selectedCategories, selectedFilesByCategory, and ALL picker states ({}); else select all categories and auto-select all files (visible=true) for file-selection ones. 'i': invert each category (deselect → delete its map entry + visible=false; select → auto-select all files + visible=true). RIGHT arrow (only if current category ∈ categoriesWithFileSelection AND its grouped list non-empty): restore saved fileCaret; if caret out-of-range or on a non-selectable row, rescan from index 0 forward to first selectable; mark this category active=true+visible=true, all others active=false; activePane='files'. Files pane (requires activeCategory): up/down move fileCaret skipping non-selectable rows (if no selectable row exists in that direction, caret stays). SPACE toggles file at caret (row must be selectable with item): COUPLING RULES — adding a file auto-adds the parent category to selectedCategories; deleting the last selected file of the category auto-removes the category. 'a': toggle-all over ALL categoryResult.items paths (not just visible rows): if all selected → deselect all (+drop category when empty), else select all (+add category). 'd': toggle all files sharing the caret row's directoryKey among VISIBLE grouped rows — if all currently selected, deselect; else select; explicitly does NOT modify selectedCategories. 'i': invert over ALL items; if any file became selected → add category; if resulting set empty → remove category. 'c' (without ctrl): copyToClipboard(path.dirname(currentFile.item.path)); on success copyStatus='Copied: {dir}' auto-cleared after 2000ms; on failure 'Failed to copy: {message}' cleared after 3000ms; previous timeout cleared first. 'm': dirExpandLimits[directoryKey] = (existing ?? 5) + 10. 'h': set limit back to 5. RIGHT on an 'expand-hint' row: same +10 expand. LEFT or BACKSPACE: setActiveCategory(null) (clears all active flags) and return to categories pane. RENDER: first line '{prefix} {bold message}', blank line; per category: '{cyan "> " if caret&categories-pane else "  "}{green ◉ if selected else dim ◯} {name.padEnd(25)} {dim (items count).padEnd(12)} {yellow size.padStart(10)}  {dim sizeGraph}'. Files render inline under a category when (isSelected && visible) || active. Pagination: when picker active, fileStart = max(0, min(fileCaret - floor(6/2), totalRows - 6)) (centered window, clamped); when visible-but-inactive, fileStart=0; fileEnd = min(totalRows, fileStart+6). Row rendering (all prefixed with 4-space INDENT + caret indicator '> ' cyan when caret on row): directory-header → dim displayName + dim ' ({totalFilesInDir})'; expand-hint → chalk.black.bgCyan('+{hiddenCount} files'); file → '{green ● if selected else dim ○} {truncateFileName(displayName,35).padEnd(35)} {magenta size.padStart(10)}'. Whole file rows are dimmed when their picker is not the active one. Footer help: categories pane → dim 'space: toggle | a: all | i: invert{ | →: see files}| enter: confirm' (files hint only when current category supports files and has rows); files pane → yellow copyStatus if set, else dim 'space: toggle | a: all | d: select dir | i: invert | m: expand | h: collapse | c: copy path | ←/backspace: back | enter: confirm'. Entire frame prefixed with '\x1B[?25l' (hide cursor).
modules.portingNotes: Built on @inquirer/core's React-like hooks (useState/useMemo/useKeypress/useRef) with full-frame re-render per keypress — in Wails this becomes a stateful GUI component, but the SELECTION STATE MACHINE (category-file coupling, cross-category isolation, per-category persisted caret/expand state surviving pane switches, 'a'/'i' operating over ALL items vs 'd' over VISIBLE rows only) is the contract to preserve; file-picker.test.ts covers exactly that pure logic. groupFilesByDirectory + truncateFileName + copyToClipboard live in src/utils/ (grouping.ts, paths.ts, clipboard.ts — not read; analyze before porting; clipboard on macOS = pbcopy or Wails runtime ClipboardSetText). ANSI cursor hide/show escapes and centered 6-row pagination are terminal-only concerns; in a GUI use scroll-into-view. Timeout-based copyStatus clearing (2s/3s) maps to a toast. Note the selection sets are keyed by absolute item.path strings — dedupe/normalization must match the scanner's emitted paths exactly.

modules.purpose: Design doc for the file-picker: architecture, constants, keymap, and selection-behavior contract.

Display pipeline in grouping.ts: groupByDirectory() groups items by parent directory sorted by size descending → applyExpandLimits() applies per-directory visibility limits → formatAsDisplayItems() flattens into directory-header / file / expand-hint rows; navigation skips non-selectable rows. Constants confirmed: FILES_PAGE_SIZE=6, DIR_VIS_CHILD_LIMIT=5, EXPAND_INCREMENT=10, FILE_NAME_WIDTH=35.
