It also pins which behaviors were intentionally untested in TS (pagination boundaries, grouping edge cases) — those need fresh test coverage in the port since visual behavior will be reimplemented.

commands.crossCutting: Shared contracts to preserve in the Go/Wails port: (1) Category model from src/types.ts (not in scope, must be ported alongside): Category {id: CategoryId, name, description, group ∈ exactly ['System Junk','Development','Storage','Browsers','Large Files'] (fixed display order), safetyLevel ∈ 'safe'|'moderate'|'risky', safetyNote?: string, supportsFileSelection?: boolean}; SAFETY_ICONS duplicated identically in clean.ts/interactive.ts/scan.ts: safe=green '●', moderate=yellow '●', risky=red '●'. (2) Scanner registry contract (src/scanners/index.ts): getAllScanners(), getScanner(id), runAllScans(opts)/runScans(ids, opts) always called with {parallel: true, concurrency: 4, onProgress(completed, total, scanner)}; scanner.clean(items[, dryRun]) returns CleanResult {category, freedSpace, cleanedItems, errors: string[]}; ScanSummary {results: ScanResult[], totalSize, totalItems}; ScanResult {category, items: CleanableItem[] ({name, path, size}), totalSize}; CleanSummary {results, totalFreedSpace, totalCleanedItems, totalErrors}. (3) Selection interchange format used by every flow: []{categoryId, items: CleanableItem[]} — cleaning always iterates categories SEQUENTIALLY even though scanning runs at concurrency 4. (4) Risky-category gating pattern: risky categories are excluded by default everywhere and re-enabled via --unsafe (clean) / --risky (interactive); risky categories additionally force per-item selection with a red safetyNote warning in clean's fallback UI. (5) Progress convention: showProgress = !noProgress && stdout.isTTY (scan adds !json); createScanProgress/createCleanProgress from utils — in Wails replace with event emission. (6) Path-safety utilities from src/utils (exists, getSize, formatSize, isProtectedPath, validatePathSafety, hasFullDiskAccess/FULL_DISK_ACCESS_HINT, copyToClipboard, truncateFileName, groupFilesByDirectory) are the guardrails before every recursive delete and MUST be analyzed/ported before any command module — every destructive path flows through validatePathSafety/isProtectedPath. (7) Consistent UX text patterns: dim '─' rules (50/60/70 chars), '[DRY RUN]' cyan prefix with early return before any deletion and before confirmation prompts, default-false confirms for destructive ops (except interactive's 'Proceed with cleaning?' which defaults true), homedir always displayed as '~'. (8) All prompts are @inquirer (confirm/checkbox/custom createPrompt) — map to Wails frontend components while keeping the pure selection-state rules testable in Go.

modules.purpose: Central type definitions and the CATEGORIES registry (16 cleaning categories with metadata).
modules.behavior: Defines: CategoryId union of exactly 16 ids: 'system-cache','system-logs','temp-files','trash','downloads','browser-cache','dev-cache','homebrew','docker','ios-backups','mail-attachments','language-files','large-files','node-modules','duplicates','launch-agents'. CategoryGroup union: 'System Junk'|'Development'|'Storage'|'Browsers'|'Large Files'. SafetyLevel: 'safe'|'moderate'|'risky'. Category{id,name,group,description,safetyLevel,safetyNote?,supportsFileSelection?}. CleanableItem{path:string, size:number(bytes), name:string, isDirectory:boolean, modifiedAt?:Date}. ScanResult{category, items:CleanableItem[], totalSize, error?}. ScanSummary{results, totalSize, totalItems}. CleanResult{category, cleanedItems:number, freedSpace:number, errors:string[]}. CleanSummary{results, totalFreedSpace, totalCleanedItems, totalErrors}. ScannerOptions{verbose?, daysOld?, minSize?}. Scanner interface: {category; scan(options?)=>ScanResult; clean(items, dryRun?)=>CleanResult}. CATEGORIES map (exact values): system-cache = 'User Cache Files' / System Junk / 'Application caches stored in ~/Library/Caches' / moderate / note 'Some apps may need to rebuild cache on next launch'. system-logs = 'System Log Files' / System Junk / 'System and application logs' / moderate / 'Logs may be useful for debugging issues'. temp-files = 'Temporary Files' / System Junk / 'Temporary files in /tmp and /var/folders' / safe. trash = 'Trash' / Storage / 'Files in the Trash bin' / safe. downloads = 'Old Downloads' / Storage / 'Downloads older than 30 days' / risky / 'May contain important files you forgot about' / supportsFileSelection:true. browser-cache = 'Browser Cache' / Browsers / 'Cache from Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Arc' / safe. dev-cache = 'Development Cache' / Development / 'npm, yarn, pip, Xcode DerivedData, CocoaPods cache' / moderate / 'Projects will need to rebuild/reinstall dependencies'. homebrew = 'Homebrew Cache' / Development / 'Homebrew download cache and old versions' / safe. docker = 'Docker' / Development / 'Unused Docker images, containers, and volumes' / safe. ios-backups = 'iOS Backups' / Storage / 'iPhone and iPad backup files' / risky / 'DANGER: You may lose important device backups permanently!'. mail-attachments = 'Mail Attachments' / Storage / 'Downloaded email attachments from Mail.app' / risky / 'May contain important documents and files'. language-files = 'Language Files' / System Junk / 'Unused language localizations in applications' / risky / 'May break apps if you switch system language'. large-files = 'Large Files' / Large Files / 'Files larger than 500MB for review' / risky / 'Review each file carefully before deleting' / supportsFileSelection:true. node-modules = 'Node Modules' / Development / 'Orphaned node_modules in old projects' / moderate / 'Projects will need npm install to restore'. duplicates = 'Duplicate Files' / Storage / 'Files with identical content' / risky / 'Review carefully - keeps newest copy by default'. launch-agents = 'Orphaned Launch Agents' / System Junk / 'Launch agents pointing to non-existent applications' / moderate / 'Removing launch agents will prevent applications from auto-starting. Only orphaned items (pointing to non-existent apps) are detected.'.
modules.portingNotes: In Go: CategoryId as string constants, Category struct, and a map[CategoryId]Category. size as int64. modifiedAt as *time.Time or time.Time+bool. For Wails, these structs will be JSON-marshaled to the frontend — pick JSON tags matching the TS field names (camelCase: safetyLevel, safetyNote, supportsFileSelection, isDirectory, modifiedAt, totalSize, freedSpace, cleanedItems, etc.) so a TS frontend can reuse the shapes.

modules.purpose: Move-based (rename) backup of items before deletion, session-timestamped under ~/.mac-cleaner-cli/backup, with 7-day retention, listing, and secure restore.
modules.behavior: BACKUP_DIR = ~/.mac-cleaner-cli/backup (join(homedir(),'.mac-cleaner-cli','backup')). BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS = 7 (constant; note config.ts has backupRetentionDays option, but backup.ts uses its own constant — the config value is NOT read here). ensureBackupDir(): session dir name = new Date().toISOString() with ALL ':' and '.' replaced by '-' (e.g. '2026-07-07T18-45-45-123Z'); mkdir -p BACKUP_DIR/<timestamp>; returns the session dir path. backupItem(item, backupDir): computes relativePath = item.path with the FIRST occurrence of homedir() replaced by literal string 'HOME' (String.replace, first match only — e.g. /Users/g/Library/Caches/x -> HOME/Library/Caches/x); backupPath = join(backupDir, relativePath); mkdir -p dirname(backupPath); then fs rename(item.path, backupPath) — a MOVE, not a copy (fast, but fails across filesystems/volumes with EXDEV); returns true/false, swallowing all errors. backupItems(items, onProgress?): creates one session dir, loops sequentially, calls onProgress(i+1, total, item) BEFORE each backup, returns {backupDir, success, failed}. cleanOldBackups(): reads entries of BACKUP_DIR; for each entry that stat()s as a directory with now - mtime > 7*24*60*60*1000 ms, rm -rf it and increment counter; per-entry errors continue; missing BACKUP_DIR silently returns 0. listBackups(): lists BACKUP_DIR entries, keeps directories, computes size via getBackupSize (recursive: sums stat().size of files only, recurses into dirs, symlinks not special-cased — entry.isFile()/isDirectory() on dirent so symlinks are skipped entirely, per-entry errors continue), returns [{path, date: stats.mtime, size}] sorted newest-first by date. restoreBackup(backupDir): first validates resolve(backupDir).startsWith(BACKUP_DIR), else returns {success:0, failed:1, errors:['Invalid backup directory: must be within the mac-cleaner-cli backup folder']}. Then recursively walks the backup dir; for each FILE (directories only recursed, empty dirs are not restored): relFromBackup = relative(resolvedBackupDir, entryPath); if it startsWith 'HOME/' -> targetPath = join(home, relFromBackup.slice(5)); if exactly 'HOME' -> skip (continue, no counter); otherwise push error `Skipping file outside HOME structure: ${relFromBackup}`, failed++. Then validateRestorePath(targetPath): rejects (error string, failed++) if resolve(targetPath) is not within home (must equal home or start with home+'/') — message `Path traversal detected: ${targetPath} resolves outside home directory` — or if the ORIGINAL targetPath string contains '..' — message `Suspicious path pattern detected: ${targetPath}`. On pass: mkdir -p dirname(targetPath); rename(entryPath, targetPath); success++; rename failure -> errors.push(`Failed to restore ${entry.name}: ${code || 'unknown error'}`), failed++. Unreadable subdirectory during walk -> errors.push(`Failed to read directory ${dir}: ${code}`), failed++. Returns {success, failed, errors}. getBackupDir() returns BACKUP_DIR.
modules.portingNotes: Key contract: backup = os.Rename (move), preserving original absolute path with home replaced by literal 'HOME' path segment; restore = reverse rename. In Go, os.Rename returns EXDEV across volumes — the TS version simply fails (backup returns false) in that case; decide whether to keep that or add a copy+delete fallback. Session timestamp format must remain filename-safe (RFC3339 with ':' and '.' -> '-'). The HOME-prefix replacement uses strings.Replace(path, home, "HOME", 1). Restore only restores files, never empty directories. The BACKUP_DIR prefix check uses plain strings.HasPrefix on the resolved path (no trailing-slash guard in TS — a sibling dir like backup-evil would pass; consider tightening in Go). Retention is a hardcoded 7 days here despite the config option existing. filepath.Rel replaces path.relative; note Node resolve() also cleans '..' but the '..' check runs against the raw string.

modules.purpose: JSON config load/validate/save with two candidate locations, hard defaults, and in-memory caching.
modules.behavior: CONFIG_PATHS in priority order: [~/.maccleanerrc, ~/.config/mac-cleaner-cli/config.json]. First readable+parseable file wins. Config fields: defaultCategories?:CategoryId[], excludeCategories?:CategoryId[], downloadsDaysOld?:number, largeFilesMinSize?:number, backupEnabled?:boolean, backupRetentionDays?:number, parallelScans?:boolean, concurrency?:number, filePicker?:boolean, extraPaths?:{nodeModules?:string[], projects?:string[]}. DEFAULT_CONFIG: {downloadsDaysOld:30, largeFilesMinSize:500*1024*1024 (524288000), backupEnabled:false, backupRetentionDays:7, parallelScans:true, concurrency:4}. Validation constraints (out-of-range values are dropped with console.warn and the default applies): downloadsDaysOld int 1..365; largeFilesMinSize int 1024..100*1024*1024*1024 (1KB..100GB); backupRetentionDays int 1..365; concurrency int 1..16; maxExtraPaths 50 (arrays truncated with .slice(0,50)). Booleans coerced via Boolean(). Category arrays filtered against VALID_CATEGORIES list, which contains only 15 ids — 'launch-agents' is MISSING from it (bug/quirk: a launch-agents entry in defaultCategories/excludeCategories is silently dropped). extraPaths validation: keep only strings, cap 50, expand leading '~/' to home, then resolve() and require the resolved path to equal or be under one of ['<home>', '/Users', '/Volumes'] (prefix+'/' or exact match); disallowed paths warn `Skipping path outside allowed directories: ${p}` and are dropped. loadConfig(configPath?): returns cachedConfig if set and no explicit path given. If configPath given: resolve it and require it under home or ~/.config (prefix match or exact), else warn 'Config path must be within home directory, using defaults' and return DEFAULT_CONFIG (cached). For each candidate path: read UTF-8; if content.length > 100*1024 (100KB) warn 'Config file too large, using defaults' and try next; JSON.parse (SyntaxError warns `Invalid JSON in config file: ${path}` and continues); validateConfig(); final = {...DEFAULT_CONFIG, ...validated} (shallow merge, validated wins); cache and return. If all fail: cache and return DEFAULT_CONFIG. saveConfig(config, configPath?): writes JSON.stringify(config, null, 2) to configPath ?? ~/.maccleanerrc and updates cache. getDefaultConfig() returns a copy of DEFAULT_CONFIG. configExists(): access() each CONFIG_PATHS entry, true on first hit. clearConfigCache() nulls the cache. initConfig(): writes to ~/.maccleanerrc a default config equal to DEFAULT_CONFIG plus extraPaths: {nodeModules:['~/Projects','~/Developer','~/Code'], projects:['~/Projects','~/Developer','~/Code']} (2-space-indented JSON) and returns the path. Note initConfig writes the '~/' strings literally to disk; expansion happens at load time.
modules.portingNotes: In Go: encoding/json with pointer fields or a defaults-then-overlay merge; TS shallow-merges the whole validated object over defaults, and validation DROPS invalid fields rather than erroring, so partial configs must work. Preserve both file locations and precedence. The missing 'launch-agents' in VALID_CATEGORIES is likely a bug — decide to replicate or fix; flag it. Config cache is a package-level singleton; in a Wails app guard it with a mutex. Warnings go to stderr/console.warn — in Wails, surface via logger or events instead. saveConfig does not create parent dirs (fine for ~/.maccleanerrc, would fail for the .config path if dir missing).

modules.purpose: Filesystem core: protected-path safety checks, size computation, directory listing/filtering, and permanent deletion with per-item error collection.
modules.behavior: Deletion strategy is PERMANENT rm -rf, NOT move-to-Trash (the backup module provides the undo path instead). PROTECTED_PATHS (never delete, prefix or exact match after resolve()): '/System','/usr','/bin','/sbin','/etc','/var/log','/var/db','/var/root','/private/var/db','/private/var/root','/private/var/log','/Library/Apple','/Applications/Utilities'. ALLOWED_PATHS override (checked FIRST; if the resolved path equals or is under one of these it is NOT protected): '/tmp','/private/tmp','/var/tmp','/private/var/tmp','/var/folders','/private/var/folders'. isProtectedPath(path): resolve, allowed-check first, then protected prefix check. validatePathSafety(path) returns error string or null: `Refusing to delete protected system path: ${path}` if protected; 'Refusing to delete root directory' if resolved === '/'; 'Refusing to delete home directory' if resolved === homedir(). exists(path): access() true/false. getSize(path): lstat; symlink -> stats.size (link itself, no follow); file -> stats.size; directory -> getDirectorySize; else/error -> 0. getDirectorySize(dirPath): recursive; readdir withFileTypes; symlink entry -> lstat size (no follow); file -> lstat size; dir -> recurse; per-entry errors continue; unreadable dir returns 0. Uses lstat size in BYTES (logical size, not disk blocks). getItems(dirPath, {recursive=false, minAge, minSize, maxDepth=10}): walks (depth counted from 0, aborts when depth > maxDepth); for each entry: lstat; if minAge set, skip when (now - mtime)/(86400*1000) days < minAge; size = symlink? lstat size : dir? getDirectorySize : file size; if minSize set, skip when size < minSize; push CleanableItem{path,size,name,isDirectory:entry.isDirectory(),modifiedAt:mtime}; recurse into non-symlink directories when recursive (note: a recursed dir is ALSO pushed as its own item, so parent+children both appear); all per-entry errors continue. getDirectoryItems(dirPath): non-recursive single-level listing with same size logic, returns [] on error — used by the file explorer. removeItem(path, dryRun=false): wrapper returning boolean (true=success) over removeItemWithError. removeItemWithError(path, dryRun=false) -> string|null: dryRun returns null immediately (counts as success, nothing deleted); validatePathSafety failure logs to console.error and returns the sentinel string 'PROTECTED'; else lstat the path FRESH (TOCTOU mitigation: re-check type immediately before delete — an attacker could swap a file for a symlink between scan and delete); if symlink -> unlink(path) only (never follow); else rm(path, {recursive:true, force:true}); success returns null; failure returns the errno code string (e.g. 'EPERM','EACCES','ENOENT') or 'UNKNOWN', and logs to console.error only for codes other than ENOENT/EACCES/EPERM. removeItems(items, dryRun, onProgress?): sequential loop; onProgress(i+1,total,item) BEFORE each removal; on success success++ and freedSpace += item.size (the pre-scanned size, not re-measured); on failure pushes {path, error} into failures[]; returns {success, failed: failures.length, freedSpace, failures}. RemoveFailure = {path:string, error:string}.
modules.portingNotes: Go: os.Lstat everywhere (never Stat) to preserve no-follow symlink semantics; os.RemoveAll for rm -rf (note: Go's RemoveAll on a symlink removes only the link, but keep the explicit lstat+os.Remove branch for clarity/TOCTOU parity); force:true means ENOENT during rm is tolerated — os.RemoveAll already returns nil for missing paths. Keep the errno-string contract ('PROTECTED', 'EPERM', 'EACCES', 'ENOENT', 'UNKNOWN') since callers key on it (e.g. suggesting FDA on EPERM); in Go extract via errors.As(&syscall.Errno) / os.IsPermission and map to those strings. resolve() = filepath.Abs+Clean (Node resolve does NOT follow symlinks; do not use filepath.EvalSymlinks). getDirectorySize is deeply recursive and slow on huge trees — a natural place for goroutine parallelism in Go, but keep results deterministic. Sequential deletion with a progress callback maps to a Wails event emit per item. freedSpace uses scan-time sizes, so numbers can drift from reality.

modules.purpose: Well-known macOS path constants, ~ expansion/contraction, traversal checks, and display truncation for paths and filenames.
modules.behavior: HOME = homedir(). PATHS constant (exact values, HOME-relative joined): userCaches=~/Library/Caches; systemCaches=/Library/Caches; userLogs=~/Library/Logs; systemLogs=/var/log; tmp=/tmp; varFolders=/private/var/folders; trash=~/.Trash; downloads=~/Downloads; documents=~/Documents; chromeCacheDefault=~/Library/Caches/Google/Chrome/Default/Cache; chromeCache=~/Library/Caches/Google/Chrome; safariCache=~/Library/Caches/com.apple.Safari; firefoxProfiles=~/Library/Caches/Firefox/Profiles; arcCache=~/Library/Caches/company.thebrowser.Browser; npmCache=~/.npm/_cacache; yarnCache=~/Library/Caches/Yarn; pnpmCache=~/Library/pnpm/store; pipCache=~/.cache/pip; xcodeDerivedData=~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData; xcodeArchives=~/Library/Developer/Xcode/Archives; xcodeSimulators=~/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Devices; cocoapodsCache=~/Library/Caches/CocoaPods; gradleCache=~/.gradle/caches; cargoCache=~/.cargo/registry; iosBackups=~/Library/Application Support/MobileSync/Backup; mailDownloads=~/Library/Containers/com.apple.mail/Data/Library/Mail Downloads; applications=/Applications. expandPath(path, allowOutsideHome=false): '~/x' -> join(HOME, x); bare '~' -> HOME; then resolve(); if the input started with '~' and !allowOutsideHome and resolved is not HOME or under HOME+'/', throw Error(`Path traversal detected: ${path} resolves outside home directory`) (catches '~/../../etc'); returns resolved absolute path (non-~ relative paths also get resolved against cwd). hasTraversalPattern(path): true if includes '../' or '/..' or equals '..' or matches regex /\/\.\.($|\/)/. SYSTEM_PATHS (used by deprecated isSystemPath; note it differs from fs.ts PROTECTED_PATHS — here '/var' is protected wholesale and the /var/log,/var/db,/var/root granularity plus /private/var/log are absent): '/System','/usr','/bin','/sbin','/etc','/var','/private/var/db','/private/var/root','/Library/Apple','/Applications/Utilities'. isSystemPath is @deprecated in favor of fs.isProtectedPath. contractPath(absolutePath): if startsWith(HOME) replace FIRST occurrence of HOME with '~' (String.replace). truncateDirectoryPath(dirPath, absolutePaths, maxLength=50): step1 display = absolutePaths ? dirPath : contractPath(dirPath); step2 if len <= maxLength return as-is; step3 split on '/' dropping empties; if parts.length <= 2 return display.substring(0, maxLength-3)+'...'; step4 middle-elision: firstPart = (parts[0]==='~' ? '~' : '/'+parts[0]); truncated = `${firstPart}/.../${lastTwoPartsJoinedWithSlash}`; if fits (<=maxLength) return it; step5 else return truncated.substring(0, maxLength-3)+'...'. Example: '/Users/mac/Documents/Projects/MyApp/src' with absolutePaths=false -> '~/Documents/.../MyApp/src' (well, elided to '~/.../MyApp/src' per algorithm — the doc example shows '~/Documents/.../MyApp/src' but code yields firstPart '~' so actual output is '~/.../MyApp/src'; implement the CODE not the comment). truncateFileName(fileName, maxLength): if fits return; ext = substring from lastIndexOf('.') only when lastDot > 0 (dotfiles like '.env' have NO ext); available = maxLength - ext.length - 3 ('...'); if available <= 0 return fileName.substring(0, maxLength-3)+'...'; else keep ceil(available/2) chars from start of the extension-less name and floor(available/2) chars from its end, joined by '...' with ext appended: `${first}...${last}${ext}`.
modules.portingNotes: Go: os.UserHomeDir(); filepath.Join. contractPath uses first-occurrence replace, effectively strings.HasPrefix + '~'+rest. Beware multi-byte runes in truncation — TS substring counts UTF-16 code units; in Go prefer []rune slicing for user-visible truncation. Node resolve() = filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(cwd, p)) for relative inputs. Keep truncateDirectoryPath's exact 5-step algorithm and the maxLength-3 hard-cut; also note the documented example in the source comment does not match the code's actual output — port the code. The PATHS map should become a struct/consts computed once at startup from the real home dir.

modules.purpose: Streaming file hashing (full and first-N-bytes partial) for duplicate detection.
modules.behavior: getFileHash(filePath, algorithm='md5'): streams the whole file through crypto createHash, resolves lowercase hex digest, rejects on stream error (destroying stream first). getFileHashPartial(filePath, bytes=1024*1024, algorithm='md5'): same but reads only byte range [0, bytes-1] inclusive (createReadStream {start:0, end:bytes-1}), i.e. first 1MB by default — used as a cheap pre-filter before full hashing in duplicate detection. Default algorithm is MD5 (speed over cryptographic strength — collision resistance is irrelevant here). Note: for files SHORTER than `bytes`, the partial hash equals the full hash of the whole file.
modules.portingNotes: Go: crypto/md5 + io.Copy(hash, f) for full; io.CopyN(hash, f, bytes) treating io.EOF/io.ErrUnexpectedEOF as success for partial (short files hash entirely). Emit hex via hex.EncodeToString. Keep 'md5' as the default and 1 MiB (1048576) as the partial size to preserve the duplicate-detection contract (equal partial hash => candidate; equal full hash => duplicate). MD5 in Go's stdlib is fine; no FIPS concerns for this use. Consider a buffered reader (bufio or 128KB buffer) to match Node stream throughput.

modules.purpose: Human-readable byte formatting/parsing (base-1024) and size threshold constants.
modules.behavior: UNITS = ['B','KB','MB','GB','TB']. formatSize(bytes): 0 -> '0 B'; else i = floor(log(bytes)/log(1024)); size = bytes/1024^i; output `${size.toFixed(i>0?1:0)} ${UNITS[i]}` — i.e. bytes show 0 decimals ('512 B'), all larger units exactly 1 decimal ('1.5 MB', '10.0 GB'). No bounds clamp: >= 1024^5 would index past the array (undefined) — inputs are assumed < 1 PB. Negative/NaN inputs unhandled (log of negative -> NaN). parseSize(sizeStr): regex /^([\d.]+)\s*(B|KB|MB|GB|TB)$/i (case-insensitive, optional whitespace between number and unit, anchored both ends); no match -> 0; else parseFloat(value) * 1024^unitIndex. SIZE_THRESHOLDS: LARGE_FILE = 500*1024*1024 (524288000), MEDIUM_FILE = 100*1024*1024 (104857600), SMALL_FILE = 10*1024*1024 (10485760).
modules.portingNotes: Go: math.Log ratio or a loop dividing by 1024. Match the exact formatting contract: 0 decimals for bytes, exactly ONE decimal for KB+ (fmt.Sprintf("%.1f %s")) — tests and UI alignment depend on it. Note toFixed rounds half-away-from-zero like %.1f, fine. Add a clamp to TB index in Go (i = min(i,4)) or replicate the unguarded behavior — clamping is the sensible fix. parseSize: regexp with (?i) flag, strconv.ParseFloat; return 0 on any parse failure (never error).

modules.purpose: Groups flat file lists by parent directory into a hierarchical display list (headers, files, expand hints) for the selection UI.
modules.behavior: DirectoryGroup{path, files:CleanableItem[], largestFileSize}. LimitedGroup{group, visibleCount, hasMore}. groupByDirectory(files): map by path.dirname(file.path); within each dir, files sorted by size DESC; groups sorted by their largestFileSize DESC (directory containing the single biggest file first — NOT by total dir size); largestFileSize = sortedFiles[0]?.size ?? 0. applyExpandLimits(groups, limits: Map<dirPath,number>, defaultLimit): per group limit = limits.get(group.path) ?? defaultLimit; visibleCount = min(limit, files.length); hasMore = files.length > limit. formatAsDisplayItems(limitedGroups, absolutePaths): emits flat GroupedFileDisplay[] in group order: (1) header {type:'directory-header', directoryPath: group.path, displayName: truncateDirectoryPath(group.path, absolutePaths) (default maxLength 50), directoryKey: group.path, selectable:false, totalFilesInDir}; (2) for each of the first visibleCount files: {type:'file', path, size, name: path.basename(file.path), displayName: same basename, directoryKey, item: the CleanableItem, selectable:true, totalFilesInDir}; (3) if hasMore: {type:'expand-hint', directoryKey, hiddenCount: files.length - visibleCount, selectable:false, totalFilesInDir}. groupFilesByDirectory(files, absolutePaths, dirExpandLimits, defaultLimit=5) chains all three. Default shows 5 files per directory before the '+N more' hint; the UI expands a dir by inserting a bigger limit into dirExpandLimits keyed by the FULL directory path and re-running.
modules.portingNotes: Go maps don't preserve insertion order — the final ordering comes from the explicit sorts (largestFileSize DESC across groups, size DESC within), so sort a slice of groups; for equal sizes JS Array.sort is stable-ish per spec (stable since ES2019) — use sort.SliceStable for parity. directoryKey is the raw absolute dir path and is the join key the TUI/GUI uses for expand state — preserve it verbatim. In Wails, GroupedFileDisplay becomes the wire struct for the file-selection view; keep type discriminator strings 'directory-header'|'file'|'expand-hint' exactly.

modules.purpose: Terminal progress bar with percentage, count, and ETA, rendered in-place via carriage return.
modules.behavior: ProgressBar(options{total, label='', showPercentage=true, showCount=true, barWidth=30}); records startTime at construction. update(current, label?) sets state and renders; increment(label?) = update(current+1). render(): percentage = min(100, round(current/total*100)); filledWidth = round(percentage/100*barWidth); bar = green '█'.repeat(filled) + dim '░'.repeat(barWidth-filled); parts joined by single space: [label truncated to 25 chars and padEnd(25), cyan] [bar] [yellow `${pct.padStart(3)}%` if showPercentage] [dim `(${current}/${total})` if showCount] [dim `~${eta}s` where eta = round((elapsedMs/current)*(total-current)/1000), shown only when elapsedMs > 1000 && current > 0 && eta > 0]. Writes `\r${output}` to stdout only when output differs from lastRender (dedupe to avoid flicker). finish(message?): overwrites the line with '\r' + spaces(lastRender.length) + '\r', then console.log(message) if given. Factories: createScanProgress(total) -> label 'Scanning...', barWidth 25; createCleanProgress(total) -> label 'Cleaning...', barWidth 25.
modules.portingNotes: In a Wails GUI this whole module dissolves: replace with runtime.EventsEmit(ctx, "scan:progress"/"clean:progress", {current,total,label,percentage,eta}) fired from the same onProgress callbacks fs.removeItems/backupItems already expose. If a CLI mode is kept, note lastRender.length counts ANSI escape codes too (the clear-line overwrite is over-long but harmless); use \r + ANSI EL (\x1b[2K) in Go instead. ETA formula: linear extrapolation elapsed/current*(remaining), floor-guarded to >0s and suppressed for the first second.

modules.purpose: Full Disk Access detection by probing a TCC-protected directory.
modules.behavior: TCC_PROTECTED_PATH = ~/Library/Safari (join(homedir(),'Library','Safari')). hasFullDiskAccess(): returns null immediately if process.platform !== 'darwin'. Otherwise attempts readdir(~/Library/Safari): success -> true (FDA granted); error with errno code 'EPERM' or 'EACCES' -> false (FDA denied — macOS TCC returns EPERM on reads of this dir without FDA, even for the owning user); any other error (e.g. ENOENT because the dir doesn't exist, e.g. Safari never launched) -> null (unknown). Tri-state result: true / false / null. FULL_DISK_ACCESS_HINT constant, exact text: 'Tip: your terminal does not have Full Disk Access, so some files cannot be scanned or removed.\n     Grant it in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access, then restart your terminal.'
modules.portingNotes: Go: runtime.GOOS != "darwin" -> nil/unknown; os.ReadDir(home + "/Library/Safari"); map error via errors.As to syscall.EPERM or syscall.EACCES -> false (os.IsPermission covers both); other errors -> unknown. Model tri-state as *bool or a small enum — a plain bool loses the 'unknown' case. IMPORTANT for the Wails port: TCC grants FDA per-APP-BUNDLE, not per-terminal — the .app produced by Wails needs its own FDA grant, and the hint text ('your terminal', 'restart your terminal') must be reworded for a GUI app (deep-link users via 'x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_AllFiles'). Alternative probe dirs if Safari's is absent: ~/Library/Mail or /Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC — but the TS contract only probes Safari and returns unknown otherwise.

modules.purpose: Stateful drill-down file explorer loop over scan results, maintaining a directory stack and cross-view selection set.
modules.behavior: runFileExplorer(initialItems, options{pageSize?}) delegates to runExplorerLoop(rootItems, selectedItems=[], options). Maintains stack of frames {path: string|null, items: CleanableItem[]}; root frame has path=null and the original scan items; message shows `Browsing: ${path ?? 'Root Scan Results'}`. Each iteration renders current frame items as choices: name = `${icon} ${nameStr} ${sizeStr}` where icon = '📂' for dirs else '📄', nameStr = item.name.substring(0,40).padEnd(40), sizeStr = yellow formatSize(item.size).padStart(10); value = item.path; checked = item currently in selectedItems (matched by path); after mapping, choices sorted directories-first (comparator returns 0 for same kind — relies on stable sort, preserves prior order within each kind). Calls explorerPrompt with pageSize (default 15), loop:false. After each prompt returns, selection sync: build set of paths visible in current view and set of paths the prompt reports checked; for each item in the current frame: if now checked and not in selectedItems -> push; if visible-but-unchecked and present in selectedItems -> splice out (selections made in OTHER directories are untouched). Then: action 'GO_UP' -> if at root, return selectedItems (exits); else pop stack. Action 'ENTER_DIR' -> newItems = await getDirectoryItems(target) (fresh single-level listing with computed sizes) and push {path: target, items}. No action (Enter) -> return selectedItems. Selections accumulate ACROSS directories; entering a dir does not auto-select/deselect children.
modules.portingNotes: This is TUI-only glue; in Wails it becomes a backend method like ListDirectory(path) (wrapping getDirectoryItems) plus frontend-held selection state — the algorithm worth preserving is the selection-sync rule: a selection is only removed when the item is VISIBLE in the current view and unchecked; unseen selections persist. Selected items keep their originally-scanned CleanableItem (path, size at listing time). getDirectoryItems recomputes directory sizes on every ENTER_DIR — can be slow on big dirs; consider async size fill in the GUI. Emoji icons and 40-char/10-char column formatting are cosmetic CLI details.

modules.purpose: Custom @inquirer/core multi-select prompt with directory navigation actions (enter/up) in addition to selection.
modules.behavior: explorerPrompt(config{message, choices:[{name,value,disabled?,isDirectory?,checked?}], pageSize=15, loop=false}) resolves to {value: string[] (checked values), action?: 'ENTER_DIR'|'GO_UP', target?: string}. Initial checked set seeded from choices with checked:true. Keybindings: Enter -> done({value: checked array}) with NO action (final submit). up/'k' -> move cursor up (clamp at 0 unless loop, which wraps to end). down/'j' -> move down (clamp at last unless loop wraps to 0). space -> toggle active item in checked set (no-op on disabled or empty list). 'a' -> toggle all: if every non-disabled value is checked, uncheck all selectable; else check all selectable. 'i' -> invert selection over selectable values. right/'l' -> only if active item isDirectory: done({value: checked, action:'ENTER_DIR', target: item.value}) — the prompt EXITS to let the caller re-render a new prompt for the subdirectory (selection state is carried through the return value). left/'h' -> done({value: checked, action:'GO_UP'}) unconditionally. Rendering per row: `${cursor} ${icon} ${label}` where cursor = cyan '❯' when active else space; icon = green '◉' checked / dim '◯' unchecked; disabled labels dimmed. Footer help line (dim): '↑↓ navigate • ← back • → enter • space select • a all • i invert • ⏎ submit'. Pagination via usePagination with pageSize/loop.
modules.portingNotes: Pure TUI; in Wails, replace with a frontend tree/list component — but preserve the interaction contract: multi-select with select-all ('a') and invert ('i'), navigate-into-dir returns control while KEEPING the checked set, and 'GO_UP' at root ends the session returning selections. The 'prompt exits on navigation' design exists because inquirer prompts can't mutate their choice list mid-flight — a GUI doesn't need that workaround. Vim keys (hjkl) were supported; nice-to-have in GUI keyboard handling.

Make sure you have `pbcopy` in your $PATH.') with cause; other Error -> `Failed to copy to clipboard: ${message}`; non-Error -> 'Failed to copy to clipboard'. macOS-only by design.

utils.crossCutting: 1) CleanableItem {path, size(bytes,int64), name, isDirectory, modifiedAt?} is THE shared currency: fs.getItems/getDirectoryItems produce it, backup/removeItems/grouping/explorer all consume it. Sizes are computed once at scan time (lstat logical size; directories recursively summed) and reused for freedSpace accounting — never re-measured at delete time. 2) Error philosophy: filesystem walks NEVER throw — every per-entry error is swallowed with continue, unreadable roots return 0/[], and only deletion/restore collect structured errors ({path, error-code} lists). Preserve this 'best-effort, keep going' contract in Go (no fatal errors from a single unreadable file). 3) Deletion is permanent rm -rf (never macOS Trash); safety comes from three layers: (a) PROTECTED_PATHS/ALLOWED_PATHS prefix checks + refuse '/' and $HOME (fs.validatePathSafety), (b) TOCTOU mitigation by re-lstat'ing immediately before delete and unlinking symlinks without following, (c) optional move-based backup (rename into ~/.mac-cleaner-cli/backup/<ISO-timestamp-sanitized>/HOME/<rel-path>, 7-day retention, restore validates paths stay under $HOME and rejects '..'). Note fs.ts PROTECTED_PATHS and paths.ts SYSTEM_PATHS have drifted (paths.ts blocks all of /var; fs.ts is granular + has /private/var/log) — fs.ts isProtectedPath is the canonical one, isSystemPath is deprecated. 4) Progress callbacks share one signature everywhere: onProgress(current 1-based, total, item), invoked BEFORE processing each item, sequential loops — maps 1:1 onto Wails EventsEmit. 5) Home-directory abstraction: literal 'HOME' path segment in backups, '~' contraction for display, '~/' expansion in config/paths with traversal guards (resolved path must stay under home; raw-string '..' checks). Every user-supplied path (config extraPaths, custom config path, restore targets) is validated by resolve + allowed-prefix whitelist ([home,/Users,/Volumes] for extraPaths; [home,~/.config] for config path). 6) Errno codes as string contract: 'PROTECTED'/'EPERM'/'EACCES'/'ENOENT'/'UNKNOWN' flow from removeItemWithError up to UI (EPERM/EACCES ties into the FDA hint) — keep exact strings in Go. 7) Display conventions: base-1024 sizes with one decimal above bytes; 50-char middle-elided directory paths ('~/.../last/two'); grouping sorted by largest-single-file DESC with 5-visible-files-per-dir default and expand hints keyed by absolute dir path. 8) Config defaults double as scanner thresholds: downloadsDaysOld=30, largeFilesMinSize=500MB (matches SIZE_THRESHOLDS.LARGE_FILE), concurrency=4, backup off by default; validation silently drops invalid fields and falls back to defaults (never errors). Two known quirks to decide on: config VALID_CATEGORIES omits 'launch-agents', and backup.ts hardcodes 7-day retention ignoring the backupRetentionDays config.

modules.purpose: Flush the macOS DNS cache via dscacheutil + mDNSResponder HUP, with root/sudo-aware execution.
modules.behavior: Exports `MaintenanceResult { success: boolean; message: string; error?: string; requiresSudo?: boolean }` (this is THE shared result contract for all maintenance tasks) and `flushDnsCache(): Promise<MaintenanceResult>`. Internals: (1) `execCommand(command, args)` wraps Node `spawn(command, args, { timeout: 10000, stdio: ['ignore','pipe','pipe'] })` — 10-second timeout, no shell (arg array, injection-safe); accumulates stdout/stderr; resolves stdout on exit code 0, otherwise rejects with `new Error(stderr || \`Process exited with code ${code}\`)`; also rejects on spawn 'error' event. (2) `canSudoWithoutPassword()` runs `sudo -n true` and returns true iff exit 0. Flow of flushDnsCache: `isRoot = process.getuid?.() === 0`. If NOT root AND `canSudoWithoutPassword()` is false → return immediately WITHOUT running anything: `{ success: false, message: 'DNS cache flush requires administrator privileges', error: 'Run with sudo: sudo mac-cleaner-cli maintenance --dns', requiresSudo: true }`. If root: run exactly `/usr/bin/dscacheutil -flushcache` then `/usr/bin/killall -HUP mDNSResponder` (two sequential commands, absolute binary paths). If not root (but passwordless sudo works): `sudo -n /usr/bin/dscacheutil -flushcache` then `sudo -n /usr/bin/killall -HUP mDNSResponder`. On success: `{ success: true, message: 'DNS cache flushed successfully' }`. On thrown error: `message: 'Failed to flush DNS cache'`; `error` = the sudo hint string `'Run with sudo: sudo mac-cleaner-cli maintenance --dns'` IF the error message contains 'Operation not permitted' OR 'sudo', else the raw error message; `requiresSudo` = true only if the error message contains 'Operation not permitted'.
modules.portingNotes: Go: use `os.Geteuid() == 0` for the root check (`process.getuid?.()` uses optional chaining because getuid is absent on Windows Node — irrelevant on macOS-only Go build but keep the nil-safety mindset). Use `exec.CommandContext` with `context.WithTimeout(10*time.Second)`; Node's spawn `timeout` sends SIGTERM on expiry. Permission-failure detection is fragile string matching on stderr ('Operation not permitted', 'sudo') — in Go prefer exit-code + typed error checks but preserve the user-facing semantics. CRITICAL for the Wails port: `sudo -n` only succeeds in a terminal where the user has a cached sudo timestamp or NOPASSWD config; from a GUI .app process it will essentially always fail. Replace the sudo strategy with `osascript -e 'do shell script "..." with administrator privileges'` or an SMJobBless/SMAppService privileged helper, and keep `requiresSudo` in the result contract so the UI can show an elevation prompt instead of a CLI hint string.

modules.purpose: Free purgeable disk/memory space by invoking Apple's /usr/sbin/purge binary.
modules.behavior: Exports `freePurgeableSpace(): Promise<MaintenanceResult>` and a DUPLICATED (copy-pasted, structurally identical) `MaintenanceResult` interface. `execCommand` is the same spawn wrapper but with `timeout: 60000` (60 s — 'purge can take a while'). The purgeable technique is solely `/usr/sbin/purge` with NO arguments — there is no dd-fill-disk trick, no APFS-specific purgeable-space reclamation, no measurement of how much was freed. Flow: `isRoot = process.getuid?.() === 0`. If root: run `/usr/sbin/purge` directly → `{ success: true, message: 'Purgeable space freed successfully' }`. If not root: FIRST try `sudo -n /usr/sbin/purge` (note: unlike dns-cache/timemachine, it does NOT pre-check canSudoWithoutPassword; it just attempts). If that throws: FALLBACK — try plain `/usr/sbin/purge` without sudo ('might work in some configurations'; purge often runs unprivileged on modern macOS). If the fallback also throws: `needsSudo = errorMessage.includes('Operation not permitted') || errorMessage.includes('Permission denied')`; return `{ success: false, message: 'Failed to free purgeable space', error: needsSudo ? 'Requires sudo. Run: sudo mac-cleaner-cli maintenance --purgeable' : errorMessage, requiresSudo: needsSudo }`.
modules.portingNotes: Order of attempts matters and differs from the other two modules: sudo-first-then-plain here vs pre-flight sudo check there — in the Go port, prefer trying plain `/usr/sbin/purge` FIRST (it usually works unprivileged and avoids GUI-sudo problems), keeping elevated execution as fallback. `purge` can legitimately take tens of seconds; use a 60 s (or longer, cancellable) context and surface progress/spinner in the Wails UI. `purge` frees inactive memory/disk caches; if the redesign wants true APFS purgeable-space reclamation, that is a different mechanism (e.g. allocating temp files to force eviction) — the TS code does NOT do that. Detection of permission failure is stderr string matching ('Operation not permitted' / 'Permission denied').

modules.purpose: List and delete all Time Machine local (APFS) snapshots via tmutil.
modules.behavior: Exports `clearTimeMachineSnapshots(): Promise<MaintenanceResult>`; imports `MaintenanceResult` from './dns-cache.js'. Constant `TMUTIL = '/usr/bin/tmutil'`. `execCommand(command, args, timeout = 30000)` — same spawn wrapper, default 30 s, but deletion calls pass 60000. Flow: (1) `isRoot = process.getuid?.() === 0`. (2) List snapshots with `tmutil listlocalsnapshotdates` (run WITHOUT sudo — listing needs no privileges). If listing throws → `{ success: false, message: 'Failed to list Time Machine snapshots', error: 'tmutil not available or Time Machine is not configured on this Mac' }`. (3) Parse output: split on '\n', trim each line, keep only lines matching the strict regex `/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{6}$/` (format like '2024-01-15-123456'); this validation is a deliberate injection guard before the dates are passed back to tmutil. (4) If 0 dates → `{ success: true, message: 'No Time Machine local snapshots found' }`. (5) If not root and `canSudoWithoutPassword()` (i.e. `sudo -n true`) fails → `{ success: false, message: 'Found ${N} snapshot(s) but cannot delete without privileges', error: 'Run with sudo: sudo mac-cleaner-cli maintenance --timemachine', requiresSudo: true }`. (6) Delete SEQUENTIALLY, one date at a time: root → `tmutil deletelocalsnapshots <date>`; non-root → `sudo -n /usr/bin/tmutil deletelocalsnapshots <date>`; each with 60 s timeout. Per-date failures are collected as strings '${date}: ${msg}' — a failure does NOT abort the loop. (7) `deleted = dates.length - errors.length`. If errors>0 AND deleted===0 → `{ success: false, message: 'Failed to delete Time Machine snapshots', error: errors[0] }` (only the first error is surfaced). Partial success → `{ success: true, message: 'Deleted ${deleted}/${total} Time Machine snapshots (${errCount} error(s))' }`. Full success → `{ success: true, message: 'Deleted ${deleted} Time Machine snapshot(s)' }` with singular/plural handling (`deleted !== 1 ? 's' : ''`).
modules.portingNotes: NOTE: this maintenance task (`--timemachine`) exists in code but is documented in neither README nor CHANGELOG — decide whether to expose it in the Wails UI. Keep the strict date regex when shelling out with user-influenced strings, even though Go's exec.Command with arg slices is already injection-safe. `tmutil deletelocalsnapshots <date>` deletes snapshots for that timestamp on ALL volumes; on recent macOS it may work without sudo for user-initiated deletion, but the TS code assumes sudo is needed — verify per-OS-version. Deletion of many snapshots is slow (60 s per date budget); in a GUI, run in a goroutine and stream per-snapshot progress events to the frontend rather than one blocking call. Aggregate-result semantics to preserve: partial success is still success:true with an 'X/Y (N error(s))' message; total failure returns only errors[0]. The comment in source documents intent: snapshots are safe to delete, macOS recreates them as needed once a backup drive is connected.

modules.purpose: Project documentation: feature set, category taxonomy, CLI usage, security posture.
modules.behavior: Facts relevant to the port: invocation is `npx mac-cleaner-cli`; flow is scan → show sizes → checkbox select → clean. 16 scan categories in three safety tiers — Safe: trash, temp-files (/tmp and /var/folders), browser-cache (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Arc), homebrew (download cache), docker (unused images/containers/volumes); Moderate: system-cache (~/Library/Caches), system-logs, dev-cache (npm, yarn, pip, Xcode DerivedData, CocoaPods), node-modules (orphaned node_modules in old projects); Risky (hidden unless `--risky`/`-r`): downloads (older than 30 days), ios-backups, mail-attachments, duplicates (keeps newest), large-files (larger than 500MB), language-files. Maintenance commands documented: `maintenance --dns` ('may require sudo') and `maintenance --purgeable' — `--timemachine` is NOT documented. Other commands: `uninstall` (app + preferences + caches + support files), `scan [--json] [--verbose]`, `clean --categories <ids> --yes | --all --yes | --dry-run | --unsafe`, `categories`, `config --init/--show`, `backup --list/--clean`. Flags: `-V/--version`, `-h/--help`, `-r/--risky`, `-f/--file-picker` (force file picker for ALL categories), `-A/--absolute-paths`, `--no-progress`. Interactive file-picker keys: up/down navigate, left back, right enter, space select, 'a' all, 'i' invert, Enter submit; file-picker-supported categories: User Cache Files, Temporary Files, System Log Files, Development Cache, Browser Cache, Homebrew Cache. Security claims to preserve: 100% offline, no telemetry, 'No Root Required — all operations run as current user' (contradicted by maintenance tasks, which do use sudo). Risky categories are always skipped in non-interactive `clean` unless `--unsafe` is passed.
modules.portingNotes: The 'No Root Required' marketing claim conflicts with the maintenance module's sudo usage — the Wails redesign should make elevation an explicit, per-task opt-in. Thresholds to carry over verbatim: downloads >30 days old, large-files >500MB, duplicates keep-newest policy. The dual-pane file picker (folder drill-down) is a headline interactive feature to reproduce as a tree/list UI in Wails. Non-interactive scan/clean with `--json` suggests keeping a headless CLI mode or JSON-emitting core library in the Go design so both GUI and automation are served by one engine.

modules.purpose: Version history 1.0.0 → 1.3.5 plus an [Unreleased] section describing in-flight behavior worth carrying into the redesign.
modules.behavior: [Unreleased] (the de-facto roadmap): (a) `scan` command — scan without deleting, `--category`, `--verbose`, `--json`; (b) `clean` command — non-interactive: `--all`, `--categories <ids>`, `--yes`, `--dry-run`, `--unsafe`; (c) visual size bars in the category picker (idea from issue #46); (d) Full Disk Access detection — interactive mode shows a ONE-TIME hint when the terminal lacks FDA instead of failing later with permission errors (issue #61); (e) clean errors now include a breakdown by errno code, e.g. 'Failed to remove 40 items (32 EPERM, 8 EACCES)', so permission issues are distinguishable from real failures. 1.3.5 (2026-06-09): fixed TOCTOU in config loading (replaced access()+readFile() with direct readFile()); unpredictable temp dirs in tests (randomBytes/mkdtemp). 1.3.3: SILENCE `EPERM` errors when removing system-owned temp files (e.g. `/var/folders/.../T/com.apple.*`) — macOS SIP/TCC returns EPERM there, expected and not actionable; previously flooded output. 1.3.0 (2025-12-23): file-picker sublist (dual-pane, directory grouping, pagination, arrow keys, copy path to clipboard, enabled by default for `large-files` and `downloads`); 12 security fixes including TOCTOU protection (re-verify file type before deletion), system path protection (block deletion of protected paths), path-traversal validation on restore paths, command-injection prevention (replaced exec() with spawn()), secure Homebrew scanner execution; config validation with bounds checking; 'proper sudo handling with privilege checking'. 1.2.0: Ko-fi donation link after successful cleanup. 1.1.9: symlink size calculation fix; graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGQUIT. 1.1.1: parallel scanner execution. 1.1.0 (2025-12-04): added uninstall command, maintenance command (flush DNS + purgeable space), config command, backup command, `--risky`, `--file-picker`, `--absolute-paths`. 1.0.0: initial 16-category interactive scanner with Safe/Moderate/Risky levels.
modules.portingNotes: Behaviors the Go port must reproduce or improve: (1) Full Disk Access detection with a one-time hint — in a Wails app this becomes a first-run permission screen; detect FDA by attempting to read a TCC-protected path (e.g. ~/Library/Mail or ~/Library/Safari) and deep-link to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access. (2) Suppress EPERM on SIP/TCC-protected paths like `/var/folders/.../T/com.apple.*` instead of surfacing them as failures. (3) Error aggregation by errno class (EPERM vs EACCES vs other) — Go: inspect syscall.Errno from os.Remove errors. (4) Security invariants from 1.3.0 to preserve: never use a shell (exec.Command with arg slices), re-verify file type immediately before deletion (TOCTOU), maintain a protected-system-paths blocklist, validate restore paths against traversal. (5) Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGQUIT mid-clean. (6) Scanners run in parallel (goroutines fit naturally). (7) Keep dry-run and JSON output modes in the core engine so GUI and automation share one code path.

maintenance.crossCutting: All three maintenance tasks share one result contract — `MaintenanceResult { success: boolean; message: string; error?: string; requiresSudo?: boolean }` — which the CLI layer renders and which the Go port should keep as a single struct (in TS it is duplicated verbatim in dns-cache.ts and purgeable.ts, with timemachine.ts importing from dns-cache; consolidate). All three use an identical private `execCommand` spawn wrapper: `spawn(cmd, argsArray, { timeout, stdio: ['ignore','pipe','pipe'] })` — never a shell (deliberate command-injection prevention from the 1.3.0 security pass), absolute binary paths (`/usr/bin/dscacheutil`, `/usr/bin/killall`, `/usr/sbin/purge`, `/usr/bin/tmutil`), stdout resolved on exit 0, rejection carrying stderr (fallback: 'Process exited with code N'). Timeouts differ per task: 10 s DNS, 60 s purge, 30 s default / 60 s per-snapshot-delete for tmutil. Sudo pattern shared by all: check `process.getuid?.() === 0` for root; otherwise probe passwordless sudo with `sudo -n true` (dns-cache and timemachine pre-flight this and bail early with `requiresSudo: true`; purgeable instead tries `sudo -n purge` then falls back to plain `purge`). Permission failures are detected by stderr substring matching ('Operation not permitted', 'Permission denied', 'sudo') and converted to actionable hints of the form 'Run with sudo: sudo mac-cleaner-cli maintenance --dns|--purgeable|--timemachine'. Exact command strings: `dscacheutil -flushcache` followed by `killall -HUP mDNSResponder` (DNS), `purge` with no args (purgeable — no dd/fill-disk technique exists), `tmutil listlocalsnapshotdates` then per-date `tmutil deletelocalsnapshots <YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS>` with dates strictly validated by /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{6}$/ (Time Machine; code-only feature, absent from README/CHANGELOG). For the Wails port the `sudo -n` strategy must be replaced (GUI processes lack sudo timestamps) with osascript 'with administrator privileges' or an SMAppService privileged helper, while preserving `requiresSudo` so the UI can drive an elevation flow.
